Working to eradicate or treat bacterial infections such as invasive pneumococcal disease, Group A Strep, and Shigella is just the beginning. Our path to success is clear and well-defined, and Vaxcyte is set up to go the distance.

WHAT we do is every bit as important as HOW we do it! Our work together is guided by four enduring core values:

*RETHINK CONVENTION: We bring creative and intellectual diversity to every facet of the work we do in order to innovate and re-innovate the way vaccines are delivered.

*AIM HIGH: We embody our collectively audacious goal to courageously make the most complex biologics ever attempted to protect humankind.

*LEAD WITH HEART: Everyone leads at Vaxcyte with a kindness-first, inclusive approach to collaboration and vigorous debate that advances our business objectives.

*MODEL EXCELLENCE:  The magnitude of our challenge requires our shared commitment to demonstrating integrity, accountability, equality and clarity across communications and decision making.

Summary:

Vaxcyte is looking for an energetic and talented individual to join our Analytical Development team. Primary responsibility for the incumbent will be to support the developmental activities currently ongoing in the laboratory as assigned.

Essential Functions:

• Contribute to method development, optimization, and qualification/validation readiness activities.

• Design and execute experiments to evaluate critical method parameters and define appropriate system suitability and control strategies.

• Troubleshoot assay and instrument performance issues using a structured approach; interpret data to identify likely root causes, implement corrective actions, and document outcomes and recommendations.

• Support and/or execute method transfer activities, including protocol preparation, training support, execution at receiving labs, and resolution of transfer issues.

• Support lab management and operations, including sample and inventory tracking.

• Author and revise analytical methods, SOPs, protocols, and technical reports; ensure clear documentation of experimental rationale, results, and conclusions for internal review and stakeholder communication.

Laboratory Operations & Instrumentation:

• Coordinate routine instrument maintenance and service activities; interface with vendors and lab management team as needed and support timely issue resolution.

• Ensure laboratory organization, cleanliness, and compliant material labeling/storage practices.

• Manage inventory of reagents, standards, and consumables; initiate procurement, track critical supplies, and support forecasting to avoid stockouts.

Team Collaboration:

• Partner effectively with cross-functional teams to define analytical plans, meet project timelines, and deliver high-quality outputs.

• Communicate experimental progress, data interpretation, and emerging risks clearly; propose mitigation plans and align next steps with stakeholders.

• Contribute to a compliant, safety-focused, and scientifically rigorous lab culture; model good documentation practices and data integrity expectations.

• Train and mentor junior staff/new team members on analytical assays, workflows, and troubleshooting; provide day-to-day technical guidance and feedback.

Analytical Testing & Data Generation:

• Perform routine and non-routine analytical testing using modern analytical methods (e.g., HPLC/UPLC, SEC, CE, UV-Vis, ELISA, electrophoresis, plate-based assays, and other biochemical/biophysical techniques).

• Execute assays in accordance with approved methods, SOPs, and applicable quality standards (GLP/GMP as applicable); identify and troubleshoot common issues.

• Perform data processing and interpretation; summarize results, trends, and potential risks, and escalate complex findings for review and decision-making.

• Maintain accurate, timely documentation in laboratory notebooks or electronic systems; contribute to clear technical communications to project and cross-functional stakeholders.

Safety & Compliance:

• Follow all Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) policies and laboratory safety practices.

• Handle chemicals and biological materials safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements.

• Ensure proper waste disposal and adherence to hazardous material handling procedures.

• Support audit and inspection readiness activities where applicable.

Requirements:

• PhD, MS or Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline. PhD with 2–5 years; MS with 7+ years; BS with 10+ years of relevant industry experience in analytical development, QC, or related field.

• Strong hands-on experience with multiple analytical techniques, such as UV-Vis, HPLC, CE, SDS-PAGE, icIEF, liquid chromatography, enzyme kinetics, colorimetric and fluorescent plate-based assays, ELISA, Western Blot, and PCR.

• Experience independently driving method development or optimization activities preferred.

• Strong knowledge of analytical chemistry/biochemistry principles with demonstrated application to assay development and control strategies.

• Proven ability to independently troubleshoot non-routine assay and instrument issues using structured root-cause analysis and data-driven decision making.

• Proficient with analytical software, data processing workflows, and statistical tools.

• Strong scientific judgment and attention to detail; consistently produces high-quality, inspection-ready documentation.

• Ability to independently plan and prioritize work, manage multiple projects, and meet timelines with minimal supervision.

• Clear and effective written and verbal communication; able to summarize complex data, present recommendations, and collaborate across functions.

• Ability to work in a laboratory environment for extended periods.

• Ability to lift up to 25 lbs.

• Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) required.

• Contribute to a positive, inclusive, and safety-focused laboratory culture.

• Other combinations of education and/or experience may be considered.

Reports to: Senior Manager, Analytical Development

Location: San Carlos, CA

Work Arrangement (may be adjusted based on business needs, job responsibilities, or changes to company policy):

Onsite (minimum of 4 days per week onsite)

Expected Contract Length: 12 months

Hourly Range: $70 - $76 (SF Bay Area). Hourly ranges for non-California locations may vary.

Equal Opportunity

Vaxcyte has an established recruitment process for all positions prior to issuing an offer for employment and we will never extend unsolicited employment offers or ask candidates to provide financial or sensitive personal information as part of the application process. All legitimate communication from Vaxcyte will come from an official @vaxcyte.com email address. Qualified and interested candidates should apply to current openings at vaxcyte.com/careers.

jobs.title: Electrical Supervisor
jobs.description:
About Riot Platforms

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. Riot’s mission is to empower the future of digital infrastructure by positively impacting the sectors, networks, and communities that we touch. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Who we are

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure.

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About the role

The Electrical Maintenance Supervisor leads the operation, maintenance, and reliability of critical electrical infrastructure supporting a data center. This role supervises maintenance personnel and contractors, ensures electrical systems are maintained in accordance with safety requirements and operational procedures, and helps sustain continuous availability of critical services.

What you'll be doing

• Supervise electrical maintenance technicians. Coordinate daily assignments, priorities, schedules, and coverage. Train, coach, and evaluate team members, and promote a strong safety culture.
• Direct preventive, predictive, corrective, and emergency maintenance for:
• Utility service entrances and switchgearMedium- and low-voltage distributionUPS systems and battery banksEmergency generators and transfer equipmentPDUs, remote power panels, and buswayTransformers, breakers, panelboards, grounding, and lighting
• Stay prepared for planned maintenance, switching, equipment failures, utility interruptions, and other critical incidents. Take part in the on-call rotation and respond to critical events.
• Review and enforce maintenance procedures, MOPs, EOPs, and SOPs. Lead electrical switching with the proper controls, approvals, documentation, and communication.
• Make sure all work follows applicable electrical codes, regulations, site safety requirements, and lockout/tagout practices.
• Work with operations, facilities, engineering, vendors, and contractors to schedule maintenance and minimize risk to data center availability. This applies primarily when the Electrical Maintenance Manager/Superintendent is absent.
• Monitor equipment condition, alarms, trends, and maintenance records to spot reliability risks and recurring issues. Investigate incidents, failures, near misses, and service-impacting events. Document findings and implement corrective actions.
• Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, equipment histories, inspections, testing, spare parts, and compliance documentation.
• Support commissioning, testing, turnover, and operational acceptance of new electrical systems, upgrades, and expansions.
• Help manage contractor performance, review work quality, verify completion, and ensure adherence to site procedures.
• Help with spare-parts planning, inventory, maintenance budgeting, and procurement of electrical materials and services.
• Other duties as assigned.

What you'll have

• Associate degree, technical diploma, apprenticeship, or equivalent experience in electrical maintenance, power systems, industrial facilities, or critical environments.
• Demonstrated experience maintaining electrical distribution and backup-power systems.
• Prior supervisory, lead, or coordination experience in a maintenance, facilities, industrial, mission-critical, or data center environment.
• Working knowledge of electrical safety practices, including arc-flash awareness, energized-work controls, and lockout/tagout.
• Ability to read and interpret one-line diagrams, electrical schematics, equipment manuals, maintenance procedures, and technical drawings.
• Strong troubleshooting skills related to power distribution, UPS systems, generators, transfer switches, breakers, and control systems.
• Ability to prioritize work effectively in a high-availability, operationally sensitive environment.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document incidents and coordinate work across teams.

Physical requirements and work environment

• Must be physically able to climb ladders and access tight or awkward spaces as required.
• Must be able to bend, reach, stoop, and pull, with good manual dexterity.
• Ability to stand, walk, and perform repetitive tasks for extended periods
• Ability to lift and move equipment as needed (50 Pounds)
• Ability to work onsite in a mining or data center environment (heat, noise, etc.)
• Exposure to high noise levels and varying temperatures

Safety Requirements

• PPE & Compliance: Strictly adhere to all site safety protocols and wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times (e.g., safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toed boots).
• Hazard Awareness: Proactively identify, report, and mitigate potential workplace hazards or unsafe conditions.
• Standards: Maintain compliance with OSHA regulations and internal safety training.
• Organization: Keep all work areas clean and free of obstructions to prevent workplace accidents.

Compensation and Benefits

• Salary commensurate with experience.
• 401(k) retirement plan: Incudes a generous company match.
• Comprehensive health coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans, HAS & FSA.
• Work-life balance: Paid time off, sick time and floating holidays.
• Wellness & lifestyle perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, employee assistance program, and more to support your life both in and out of work.

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Systems/Technology Analyst - Financial Management System Consolidation Analysis & Roadmap
jobs.description:
Job Description

CSCI is seeking an experienced Systems/Technology Analyst to support a Financial Management System Consolidation Analysis and Roadmap initiative. These professionals will play a critical role in evaluating existing financial management technology environments, identifying system and integration opportunities, assessing modernization approaches, and developing actionable implementation roadmaps.

The ideal candidate possesses a unique blend of enterprise architecture, systems analysis, financial management, and technology transformation expertise. This role requires the ability to translate business needs into technical solutions while helping stakeholders understand technology implications, risks, dependencies, and modernization opportunities.

Responsibilities

• Assess current-state financial management systems, applications, integrations, databases, and technical architecture

• Conduct enterprise application portfolio analyses to identify redundancies, modernization opportunities, and consolidation strategies

• Evaluate system interfaces, APIs, middleware platforms, data exchanges, and integration dependencies

• Gather and analyze business requirements and translate them into technical requirements, solution designs, architecture recommendations, and implementation approaches

• Develop current-state and future-state architecture models, technology assessments, and modernization strategies

• Analyze data structures, data flows, master data management approaches, and reporting environments

• Identify technology risks, technical debt, interoperability challenges, and migration considerations

• Support the development of financial management system consolidation roadmaps and transition strategies

• Create implementation planning artifacts, including Data Migration Plans, System Transition Strategies, Decommissioning Checklists, Integration Approaches, Technical Sequencing Plans

• Collaborate with functional analysts, enterprise architects, business stakeholders, and government leadership to align technical solutions with mission requirements.

• Prepare executive briefings, assessments, technical recommendations, and decision-support documentation

• Support cloud migration, enterprise architecture, and technology transformation initiatives

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related field

• 10+ years of experience supporting systems analysis, enterprise architecture, technology modernization, or digital transformation initiatives

• Demonstrated experience assessing enterprise systems, technical architectures, application portfolios, and integration environments

• Experience evaluating: Financial Management Systems, Enterprise Applications, APIs and Web Services, Databases and Data Architecture, Integration Platforms, Cloud-Based Solutions

• Strong understanding of systems analysis methodologies and solution architecture principles

• Experience translating business requirements into technical requirements, architecture designs, and implementation recommendations

• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage both business and technical stakeholders

• Proven analytical and problem-solving abilities

• Creativity and adaptability in problem-solving

• Ability to work with clients to understand their needs

• Strong organizational and time-management skills

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Professional presence

Preferred Skills

• Experience supporting Department of Defense (DoD), Defense Agencies, or other Federal Government organizations

• Familiarity with federal financial management systems and technology environments

• Experience supporting ERP solutions such as SAP, Oracle, Workday, PeopleSoft, or similar enterprise platforms

• Experience with cloud technologies and modernization initiatives, including AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud

• Knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks such as TOGAF, FEAF, DoDAF, or Zachman

• Experience supporting system consolidation, migration, modernization, or shared services transformation initiatives

• Understanding of system lifecycle management, governance processes, and modernization best practices

• Relevant certifications such as TOGAF, PMP, AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Azure Solutions Architect, SAFe, or similar credentials

• Enterprise Systems Analysis • Experience evaluating financial management systems, application portfolios, interfaces, APIs, databases, and technical architectures • Ability to identify redundancies, integration challenges, technical risks, and modernization opportunities across complex environments • Experience conducting technology assessments and system rationalization efforts

• Business-to-Technology Translation • Ability to gather and analyze business requirements and convert them into technical requirements and solution designs • Experience developing architecture recommendations, integration strategies, data models, and future-state technology solutions • Proven ability to communicate effectively with both business and technical audiences

• Technology Modernization & Roadmap Development • Experience supporting application modernization, cloud adoption, technology transformation, and enterprise architecture initiatives • Ability to assess current-state environments and develop future-state technology roadmaps aligned with business objectives • Experience establishing implementation priorities, sequencing dependencies, and identifying transformation milestones

• Technology Implementation Planning • Experience developing implementation guidance and transition planning documentation • Ability to create data migration strategies, system cutover plans, decommissioning checklists, and technology transition frameworks • Experience supporting large-scale system deployment and migration efforts

• Federal Financial Management • Understanding of federal accounting, audit readiness, financial reporting, internal controls, compliance requirements, and financial operations • Experience supporting DoD, Defense Agencies, or other federal organizations preferred

• Ability to work in a team environment, as well as independently

• Strong customer and vendor relationship skills

• Demonstrated ability to comply with data standards and policies

• Motivation to learn new technologies and methodologies that demonstrate value

• Past experience working with a federal government agency

• Department of War experience is a plus!

About CSCI

CSCI is an award-winning information technology and financial management consulting firm founded on one simple philosophy: “Do what is right, always.” We apply this philosophy across all elements of our growing business, from delivering world-class services for customers to providing an environment where associates thrive both personally and professionally. At CSCI, work and fun aren’t diametrically opposed!

At CSCI, our goal is to hire people with proven track records and retain them with an energizing, diverse company culture. We value each associate’s natural drive to excel, and we provide them with the freedom to do things their way. jobs.title: Operator III
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

The Operator III is responsible for supporting the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of a reciprocating engine-based power generation facility consisting of multiple engine-generator units and associated balance-of-plant (BOP) systems. This role performs routine operational activities, monitors plant equipment, and assists in maintaining optimal plant performance while ensuring compliance with all safety, environmental, and operational requirements.

The Operator III works closely with the Shift Supervisor, Instrumentation & Electrical (I&E) Technicians, Maintenance Technicians, OEM representatives, contractors, and vendors to support plant availability, equipment reliability, commissioning activities, startup and shutdown operations, troubleshooting, and planned outages. This position requires strong mechanical aptitude, attention to detail, sound judgment, and a commitment to safe work practices in a high-reliability power generation environment.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Safely start, stop, operate, and monitor engine-generator packages and all associated auxiliary equipment in accordance with OEM specifications, plant procedures, and operating limits.
• Monitor plant equipment through the control system and field inspections to ensure safe and reliable operation.
• Adjust operating parameters and setpoints within approved OEM and plant guidelines to optimize performance, efficiency, and equipment reliability.
• Conduct routine equipment inspections and document operating conditions, equipment status, and abnormalities.
• Identify, troubleshoot, and report equipment malfunctions or abnormal operating conditions to the Shift Supervisor.
• Assist with plant startups, shutdowns, commissioning activities, and planned maintenance outages.
• Coordinate with Maintenance and I&E personnel to safely isolate equipment and return systems to service following maintenance activities.
• Complete operating logs, shift reports, inspections, and other required documentation accurately and in a timely manner.
• Participate in OEM and company training programs to develop a thorough understanding of plant systems, operating procedures, and equipment capabilities.
• Follow all company safety policies, environmental regulations, permit-to-work procedures, lockout/tagout (LOTO), confined space, and other safe work practices.
• Maintain high standards of housekeeping throughout the facility to promote a safe and organized work environment.
• Assist contractors, OEM representatives, and vendors while work is performed on site.
• Respond appropriately to plant alarms, emergency situations, and abnormal operating conditions.
• Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance plant safety, reliability, and operational efficiency.
• Perform other duties as assigned by the Shift Supervisor or Plant Management.

Work Environment:

• Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.
• Ability to work around high-voltage equipment, rotating machinery, elevated noise levels, and hot surfaces while following all applicable safety procedures.

Education/Experience/Background:

• High School Diploma or GED required.
• Previous experience in industrial operations, manufacturing, utilities, oil and gas, or power generation is preferred but not required.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Basic understanding of mechanical equipment, pumps, compressors, engines, valves, and auxiliary systems.
• Ability to read and interpret operating procedures, equipment manuals, and technical documentation.
• Basic computer skills and ability to use plant monitoring and reporting systems.
• Strong communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.
• Commitment to maintaining a safe work environment.
• Ability to recognize abnormal equipment conditions and respond appropriately.
• Mechanical aptitude with the ability to learn complex plant systems.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
• Ability to prioritize tasks in a fast-paced operating environment.
• Willingness to work rotating shifts, weekends, holidays, overtime, and respond to emergency callouts as required.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Technical training or coursework in power generation, industrial operations, mechanical systems, or a related field preferred.

Physical Requirements:

• Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
• Ability to climb stairs and ladders and work at elevated heights.
• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.
• Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, and flame-resistant clothing.

Benefits: Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

Disclaimer: The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law.

jobs.title: Head of Analytical Development & Quality Control
jobs.description:
The Head of Analytical Development & Quality Control will provide strategic and operational leadership for analytical development, characterization, method validation, transfer, and quality control activities supporting a growing pipeline of small molecule Oral  Dose and parenteral Drug Product programs.  The incumbent will have deep experience in analytical activities required to support early-stage to late-stage drug substance as well as  oral solid dose and parenteral drug products. Additional experience in antibody/ADC manufacturing-focused analytical activities is desirable. This individual will be responsible for operating in a 100% outsourced environment to establish and will manage phase-appropriate analytical strategies from preclinical through commercialization, overseeing external analytical operations, and ensuring compliance with global regulatory expectations and GMP requirements for assigned programs.

As a key member of the Technical Operations team, this leader will collaborate cross-functionally with Medicinal Chemistry, Toxicology, Clinical Pharmacology, Drug Substance, Drug Product, , Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, and external CDMOs/CROs/consultants to advance programs efficiently through development milestones while building scalable analytical and quality control capabilities for a rapidly growing organization.

Key Responsibilities

Analytical Development Leadership

• Build and lead a small team of analytical development and quality control chemists capable of developing and executing phase-appropriate analytical method development and testing strategies and activities supporting Chemical and Drug Product development and eventual commercialization of the Treeline portfolio, including:

• Phase-appropriate small molecule drug substance method development and testing

• Phase-appropriate small molecule oral dose drug product method development and testing (tablets, capsules, gelcaps, pediatric formulations, etc.)

• Phase-appropriate small molecule oral dose drug product intermediate method development and testing (e.g. amporphous solid dispersions)

• Provide technical oversight for development, qualification, validation, and lifecycle management of analytical methods.

• Ensure analytical methods support process development, formulation development, manufacturing, release testing, and regulatory submissions.

Quality Control Oversight

• Establish and lead QC strategies across clinical manufacturing operations

• Oversee external GMP testing activities including raw materials, IPCs, release testing and stability programs.

• Ensure timely release and disposition support for clinical materials.

• Manage investigations involving OOS, OOT, deviations, and laboratory events.

Regulatory and Quality Support

• Author and review analytical sections of regulatory submissions including: INDs, IMPDs, BLAs, NDAs, and CTAs.

• Ensure analytical approaches align with ICH, FDA, EMA, and other global regulatory expectations.

• Support establishment of specifications and analytical control strategies throughout the product lifecycle.

• May participate in regulatory agency interactions and inspections.

• Ensure compliance with cGMP, GLP, GCP, and data integrity requirements.

• Partner closely with Quality Assurance to maintain inspection readiness.

• Support audits of contract testing laboratories and manufacturing partners.

External Partner Management

• Manage relationships with contract laboratories and CDMOs.

• Oversee method transfers, validation activities, and technical governance of external laboratories.

• Establish performance metrics and ensure delivery against development and manufacturing timelines.

• Evaluate/implement new technologies/outsourced capabilities as needed.

Required Qualifications

Education

• Ph.D./MS in Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering, or related scientific discipline preferred.

Experience

• 12+ years (Ph.D.)15+ years (MS) of progressive pharmaceutical or biotechnology analytical development experience.

• Demonstrated deep experience in analytical development activities supporting Small molecule Drug Substance and Drug Product development and manufacturing with emphases on oral solid dose, parenteral, and pediatric formulations.

• Demonstrated success in developing and validating discriminating dissolution methods for 1+ OSD tablets.

• Proven track record advancing products from early development through late-stage clinical development and/or commercialization.

• Demonstrated success working with CDMOs and global development partners.

• Additional experience in development and implementation of analytical methods to support antibody/ADC manufacturing is desirable.

Technical Expertise

Strong working knowledge of:

• Analytical method development and validation

• Stability programs and specification setting

• Quality control laboratory operations

• GMP analytical testing

• Small molecule drug substance characterization and phase-appropriate method development.

• Oral solid dose characterization and phase-appropriate method development, including discriminatory dissolution method development

• ADC analytical characterization

• Experience with Biologics testing methodologies desirable

• Strong command of and facility working with relevant ICH quidances

• Regulatory submissions and health authority interactions

Leadership Competencies

• Strategic thinker with strong business and scientific acumen.

• Excellent project management and organizational skills.

• Strong communication and influence skills across scientific, quality, regulatory, and program teams

• Ability to travel (20%) to CDMO domestic and international sites.

• Fluency with standard computer software packages (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project), iStability, and JMP (or similar statistical tools).

• High level of personal integrity, commitment to excellence and to our patients.

• Experience in developing and commercializing drugs for oncology is preferred.

This position is classified as exempt. The anticipated annual base salary range for the role is $234,500 to $286,338. The final base salary offered to the successful candidate will be dependent upon several factors that may include but are not limited to the type and length of experience within the job, and other factors. Treeline Biosciences is a multi-state employer, and this salary range may not reflect positions that work in other cities or states.

Please be aware of recruitment fraud and related job scams, where scammers present themselves as recruiters but are seeking to steal money or personal information. Keep the following in mind to protect yourself:

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Data De-Identification
jobs.description:
ABOUT TONIC.AI

Tonic.ai http://Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, UnitedHealth Group, Qualcomm, Commonwealth Bank, and Mercor. Our newest line of business takes that work somewhere it hasn't gone before: company operating data. Email, chat, tickets, documents, code, CRM and HR records are some of the most valuable training data left for AI labs, and almost none of it can change hands until the people in it are protected.



We sit between the company that owns the data and the lab that wants it, as the independent third party. We take in the corpus, find the people and organizations referenced across all of those systems, give each real identity one consistent synthetic replacement, rebuild every file in its original format, and deliver the result with a written report on how it was done. The data still reads like a company doing its work, which is what makes it worth training on.




WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW

Demand is running ahead of our capacity to deliver. Labs are buying, data owners are selling, and the buyers want datasets in days to weeks, not quarters. The technology can meet that timeline. What turns it into a delivered dataset is an engineer who can take a messy, half-documented corpus from a new client, get it through the pipeline, catch what breaks, and ship something both sides will sign off on.



That's this job. You’ll be one of the first engineers dedicated to this business, working directly with our technical founders, data science team and platform engineers, and getting close to the frontier AI labs that are the end buyers of this data.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the delivery of client de-identification projects, from the first look at the raw data to a dataset the client accepts.

 - Run each corpus through our de-identification pipeline and check the output for accuracy: missed entities, wrong replacements, identities merged or split incorrectly, files that won’t rebuild.

 - Diagnose problems as they appear. Where you can, fix them for the whole solution or for the one case. Where you can’t, understand the issue well enough to explain it clearly to the engineer who can.

 - Rerun the pipeline, confirm the fix worked, then move on to the next step, which often includes working with our annotation team to validate quality.

 - Build and adjust the ingestion and transformation steps that turn raw exports (mailboxes, chat archives, document dumps, ticketing systems, databases) into processed, ready-to-use datasets.

 - Write code that gets merged, within the guardrails of our existing platform, including custom handling for client-specific one-offs.

 - Run reconciliation checks so file counts and content tie from ingest to delivery.

 - Contribute to the technical sections of the client report: what was treated as sensitive, what was kept and why, how each file type was handled, and known limitations.

 - Walk clients through what was done and the resulting data, alongside Tonic’s founders at first and on your own as you grow.

 - Turn every one-off fix into something reusable: documentation, runbooks, and improvements to the product.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A bachelor’s degree in a technical field (computer science, engineering, math, statistics, physics or similar).

 - Several years of hands-on work in data engineering, backend engineering, or a solutions/forward-deployed role where you shipped production systems for customers.

 - Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading and debugging other people's code.

 - Real experience with at least one major cloud (AWS, GCP or Azure): storage, compute, IAM, networking, and the security controls clients will ask about.

 - Experience processing large volumes of unstructured and semi-structured data. You know what a PST, an mbox, a Slack export or a 40-tab spreadsheet looks like on the inside, or you can figure it out in an afternoon.

 - A record of delivering complex projects on short timelines, measured in days and weeks.

 - Clear communication with very different audiences. You can walk a client's engineer through a pipeline failure in the morning and explain a tradeoff to a senior executive in the afternoon.

 - Self-direction. You'll often be the only engineer on an engagement, and you'll need to make sound calls without waiting for someone to tell you what to do.

 - AI-native habits. You use AI coding tools, agents and LLMs in your daily work as a matter of course, and you have opinions about where they help and where they don't.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with model inference or ML pipelines.

 - Exposure to processing unstructured or semi-structured data (email, chat exports, documents).

 - Interest in working close to frontier AI labs and the training-data ecosystem.

 - Experience at an early-stage company or on a new product line.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first month, you'll learn the platform and the delivery process and run part of a live engagement alongside the team. By the end of your first quarter, you'll be running engagements on your own, from scoping to delivery, and the runbooks and tooling you've written will have made the second and third ones faster than the first. After that, you'll help decide how this function grows, including who we hire next.




WHY JOIN

 - You’ll be early in a fast-growing business solving a problem the AI industry doesn’t yet have a good answer for.

 - You’ll work alongside technical founders, with a direct line from what you see in the field to what gets built.

 - You’ll get close to the frontier AI labs and build experience at the center of the training-data market.

 - The work matters beyond any one deal: getting company data to labs without exposing the people in it is a problem the whole industry has to solve.

 - Competitive compensation and equity.

jobs.title: Regional Director, Outreach (FL, Orlando)
jobs.description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

This role is a rare chance to lead the go-to-market efforts for one of the fastest growing startups in the healthcare industry. You'll be granted an unparalleled level of responsibility, as your efforts will define how we open and win in new markets. As a Regional Director, it will be your responsibility to manage a state-wide or multi-state region, supporting the Directors and Managers that represent Charlie Health in the region. You'll work hand-in-hand with our leadership team to identify patient referral sources, build relationships with clinical partners, and facilitate admissions for hundreds of at-risk youth. You'll obsess (in a healthy way) over ensuring that every possible patient, parent, and provider is aware of Charlie Health’s programs.

Our team is comprised of passionate, forward-thinking professionals eager to take on the challenge of the mental health crisis and play a formative role in providing live-saving solutions. We are looking for a candidate who is inspired by our mission and excited by the opportunity to build a business that will impact millions of lives in a profound way.

Responsibilities

• Support new admissions goals; this role will be responsible for the team’s overall performance which may include carrying a book subject to current team size and growth

• Manage and lead a team of Outreach Directors and Managers in a specific region, ensuring that regional performance goals are met or exceeded

• Measure and own KPIs across your region, reporting upwards on a monthly basis

• Develop and operationalize GTM strategy for efficient new market penetration

• Create, build, and manage relationships with referral sources across priority markets

• Lead meetings with patients, parents, and providers to uncover needs, address barriers to treatment, and cement community partnerships

• Design strategies to better support and engage referral partners across different channels

• Deepen Charlie Health’s penetration across existing partnerships

• Attend and lead various educational meetings, marketing presentations, and networking events both in person and via conference call

• Synthesize and share market feedback from partners, patients, and stakeholders to inform go-forward marketing and product strategies

• Work closely with internal partners including marketing, product, client success, and legal to deliver on GTM goals

Requirements

• Must be based in Orlando, FL

• 6-10+ years of business development experience, including 2-3+ years of experience in sales leadership

• Experience in healthcare is a plus

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Google Suite, CRM (Salesforce preferred), scheduling, and video conferencing technologies

• Work authorized in the United States and native or bilingual English proficiency

• Demonstrated track record of top-tier performance in the development, maintenance, and growth of customer accounts in a B2B / outreach setting

• Experience managing, coaching, and motivating a business development team

• Experience measuring, analyzing, and being accountable to well-defined sales metrics/KPIs

• Exceptional interpersonal, relationship-building, and listening skills, with a natural, consultative style

• Ability to energize, communicate, and build rapport at all levels within an organization

• Ability to travel locally (within ~1 hour driving distance) for meetings with potential referral partners

• Must have reliable transportation, a valid driver's license, and the ability to drive up to 1-hour each way on a regular basis

• Strong project management skills, with a demonstrable ability to corral and manage details in a fast-paced, fluid environment

• Expert in advising, presenting to, and persuading senior corporate personnel

Benefits

Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Additional Information

The total target base compensation for this role will be between $125,000 and $165,000  per year at the commencement of employment. In addition to base compensation, this role offers a target performance-based bonus. Please note, pay will be determined on an individualized basis and will be impacted by location, experience, expertise, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations. Further, cash compensation is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may include stock options and other Charlie Health-sponsored benefits.

Our Values

• Connection: Care deeply & inspire hope.

• Congruence: Stay curious & heed the evidence.

• Commitment: Act with urgency & don’t give up.

Charlie Health will never ask you to pay a fee or download software as part of the interview process with our company. In addition, Charlie Health will not ask for your personal banking information until you have signed an offer of employment and completed onboarding paperwork that is provided by our People Operations team. jobs.title: Senior Architect (Licensed Building Architect), Data Centers - Remote (U.S.)
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Lead Architect with deep expertise in the design and delivery of colocation and hyperscale cloud data center facilities. The ideal candidate is a licensed architect with a proven track record of leading complex, mission critical projects from concept to commissioning. This role will play a key part in shaping the architecture of high-performance, secure, and scalable data center environments to meet the evolving demands of top tier cloud and colocation clients.

This position offers the flexibility of a remote work schedule and can be based from a variety of locations in the US where AECOM has an office.

Although the position is primarily remote periodic travel may be required for client meetings, key project milestones, onsite collaboration sessions, or other business‑critical activities. Travel is expected to be occasional and scheduled in advance.

AECOM is a leader in the global data center consulting industry with robust teams in the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.  In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with our teams around the world on high-profile, fast-paced data center projects for global clients.  This is a hands-on, client-facing role with an opportunity for upward career mobility.

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead architectural design for large scale hyperscale cloud data center and colocation projects, from early concept through construction administration and closeout.
• Collaborate with internal engineering disciplines, construction teams, and external stakeholders to develop fully coordinated and integrated design solutions.
• Develop and review drawings, specifications, and technical documentation, ensuring compliance with codes, standards, and client design guidelines.
• Manage coordination with consultants, contractors, and permitting authorities to support project delivery and regulatory compliance.
• Serve as the architectural subject matter expert for hyperscale and colocation clients, ensuring operational efficiency, scalability, and reliability in facility design.
• Mentor and guide junior architects and designers, fostering technical excellence and design innovation.
• Maintain and apply knowledge of industry best practices and data center design trends.
• Support business development, proposal writing, and conceptual architectural designs for new pursuits.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and or education.
• Demonstrated experience with colocation and hyperscale data center projects.
• Experience with and knowledge of building codes, mission critical infrastructure standards, and data center design requirements.
• Experience in BIM ACC (Revit), AutoCAD, and related design tools.

Preferred Qualifications:

• 5+ years of experience working with hyperscale client standards and colocation facility delivery models.
• Active U.S. Architectural license.
• LEED accreditation or equivalent sustainable design credentials.
• Experience working in fast paced, global project environments.
• Extensive experience working with permitting authorities and AHJs.
• Excellent leadership, communication, and project management skills.
• Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary and geographically diverse teams.

• Relocation is not available for this role
• Sponsorship for U.S. employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
• THIS POSTING IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND AECOM INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY APRIL 5, 2027.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.description:
What You Get To Do:

A Direct Support Professional (DSP) caregiver provides direct support, positive direction, instruction, and assistance to individuals with mental, intellectual & developmental, and physical disabilities.  The ultimate goal is to empower individuals with disabilities to live as independently and comfortably as possible while maintaining their dignity and respect. Floats fill in at different programs around Lake and Porter County. The schedule is varied (days/evenings/weekends).

• Provide hands-on assistance, encouragement, mentoring, and guidance.
• Coordinate services for the individuals served, including finance, medical, recreation, program services, family contact/involvement, education, and household management.

jobs.title: Staff Applied AI Engineer, Agentic Systems
jobs.description:
ABOUT BEACON AI

We’re a fast-moving team of aviators, engineers, and operators building an AI platform to make flying safer, more efficient, and more capable. Backed by top investors, we’ve secured a dozen Department of Defense contracts and partnered with major airlines to deliver mission-critical systems. We operate without silos or heavy processes. Small, focused teams own what they build, ship quickly, and learn fast, pushing the boundaries of how humans and AI work together in aviation.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

At Beacon AI, we're building AI-powered systems that help aviation professionals navigate complex, high-stakes operational decisions.

This role sits at the intersection of agentic AI, information retrieval, and production software engineering. We build systems that reason over diverse sources of information, use tools to investigate problems, and produce reliable, explainable results.

We're looking for engineers who can think critically about how these systems should work, design their underlying information and orchestration architectures, and take them from experimental prototypes to dependable production services.




DESIGN AND BUILD AGENTIC SYSTEMS

 - Design and implement agent architectures involving tool use, planning, orchestration, state management, and memory.

 - Develop effective context engineering strategies, balancing relevant information, model capabilities, latency, and cost.

 - Make thoughtful architectural decisions about when to use autonomous agents, explicit workflows, conventional algorithms, or combinations thereof.

 - Design tool interfaces and structured model interactions that support reliable, inspectable behavior.


TURN COMPLEX INFORMATION INTO USABLE KNOWLEDGE

 - Develop an understanding of complex document collections and data sources: their structure, semantics, authority, relationships, and scope.

 - Translate domain knowledge into effective retrieval systems, structured representations, and agent-accessible tools.

 - Apply information retrieval, information extraction, and knowledge modeling techniques to heterogeneous structured and unstructured data.

 - Design strategies for handling temporal relevance, provenance, conflicting evidence, and incomplete information.


EVALUATE AND IMPROVE AI BEHAVIOR

 - Develop rigorous evaluations for AI-powered systems, including representative datasets, human annotations, automated assessments, and targeted failure analysis.

 - Investigate system-level failures across retrieval, context construction, reasoning, tool execution, and final outputs.

 - Experiment with alternative architectures, models, and prompting strategies, using empirical results to guide decisions.

 - Help establish engineering practices for measuring and improving the reliability of agentic systems.


BUILD SYSTEMS THAT WORK IN PRODUCTION

 - Develop reliable services and asynchronous workflows with attention to concurrency, fault tolerance, observability, and maintainability.

 - Integrate model inference, retrieval systems, and external data services into production applications.

 - Build and operate containerized workloads and cloud infrastructure.

 - Collaborate with engineers and domain experts to translate complex operational requirements into working systems.
   
   


AREAS OF SPECIALIZATION

Applied AI is a broad discipline. We don't expect every candidate to have deep expertise in every part of the stack.

We particularly encourage candidates with substantial experience in one or more of the following areas:

 - Agentic systems and context engineering: Agent orchestration patterns, planning and execution, tool-use architectures, persistent and transient memory, and context management.

 - Information retrieval and knowledge representation: Semantic and structured retrieval, information extraction, document understanding, entity and relationship modeling, and knowledge-driven tool design.

 - AI evaluation and reliability: Evaluation methodology, benchmark and dataset construction, human and model-based assessment, statistical analysis, and systematic failure characterization.

 - Model adaptation and inference optimization: Fine-tuning, model selection, inference serving, quantization, batching, and performance optimization.

We value candidates who bring genuine depth to at least one of these areas, along with the curiosity and engineering judgment to work effectively across disciplinary boundaries.




WHAT WILL MAKE YOU SUCCESSFUL

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals. You write maintainable production code, reason about system architecture, and understand testing, debugging, and operational reliability.

 - Substantive applied AI experience. You've worked on AI systems beyond basic model API integrations and can explain their architecture, tradeoffs, limitations, and observed behavior.

 - Information modeling instincts. You can understand a new domain, identify its important entities and relationships, and design software abstractions that reflect how its information is actually used.

 - Experimental discipline. You test assumptions, measure results, investigate failure modes, and use evidence to guide technical decisions.

 - Independent technical judgment. You can evaluate alternative approaches, recognize unnecessary complexity, and make appropriate tradeoffs.

 - Clear communication. You can discuss technical decisions with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and domain experts.

We care more about demonstrated technical understanding and the quality of your engineering work than familiarity with any particular AI framework.




OUR TECHNOLOGY ENVIRONMENT

Our systems primarily use Python, LangGraph, BAML, AWS Bedrock, PostgreSQL/pgvector, and event-driven AWS infrastructure.

Experience with these technologies is helpful but not required. We're more interested in your understanding of the underlying concepts and ability to work effectively with unfamiliar tools.




ESPECIALLY VALUABLE EXPERIENCE

 - Aviation, aerospace, or another technically complex, safety-critical domain.

 - Computational linguistics, NLP, information science, or knowledge representation.

 - Designing systems that reason over technical documentation, regulations, or heterogeneous operational data.

 - Developing or operating distributed, event-driven, and containerized services.

 - Building AI systems in which traceability, evidence, and human oversight are important.




EXAMPLES OF PROBLEMS YOU MIGHT WORK ON

 - Design an agentic workflow that identifies operational risks from aviation weather, airspace restrictions, aircraft-specific information, and regulatory guidance.

 - Develop retrieval and tool interfaces that allow agents to navigate multiple information sources while preserving source authority, provenance, and temporal relevance.

 - Build an evaluation framework that measures the factual completeness, correctness, and operational relevance of AI-generated analyses.

 - Investigate when an agent should perform additional research, use a specialized tool, or terminate its investigation.

 - Improve the reliability, latency, and cost of a multi-stage AI workflow through architectural changes informed by evaluation results.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR IN YOUR APPLICATION

We'd be particularly interested in hearing about an AI system you've designed or meaningfully improved, including the engineering decisions you made, the alternatives you considered, and how you determined whether the system was successful.

We value thoughtful technical work over the number of frameworks or models listed on a résumé.

Work Location
This is a hybrid role based in San Carlos, CA, with 3+ days per week onsite and the option to work remotely on remaining days.

Perks & Benefits (Full-Time Employees)

 - Healthcare: 100%* of employee medical premiums covered; 25% for dependents

 - Time Off: 3 weeks PTO plus 13+ paid company holidays

 - 401(k): Offered (no current employer match, but we are committed to enhancing this benefit in the future)

Due to U.S. export control regulations, we can only hire U.S. Persons (U.S. citizens, Green Card holders, lawful permanent residents, or individuals granted asylum or refugee status). We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or support visa transfers. All work must be performed in the United States.


Beacon AI is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We prohibit harassment or discrimination of any kind in the workplace and comply with all applicable federal, state, and local employment laws.

jobs.title: Copy of Electrical Assistant Supervisor
jobs.description:
About Riot Platforms

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. Riot’s mission is to empower the future of digital infrastructure by positively impacting the sectors, networks, and communities that we touch. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Key attributes we're looking for

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure.

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About this role

The Electrical Assistant Supervisor supports the Electrical Maintenance Supervisor in directing daily electrical maintenance at a mission-critical data center. This role leads and mentors Tier 1–3 technicians, performs hands-on maintenance and troubleshooting of critical power systems such as generators, UPS, switchgear, transformers, and PDUs, and serves as the first point of escalation for complex issues. The Assistant Supervisor enforces LOTO, arc flash, and NFPA 70E and NFPA 70B safety standards, oversees contractors, maintains CMMS records, responds to power alarms and emergencies, and directs shift operations when the primary supervisor is offsite.

What you’ll be doing

• Assign daily work, review shift schedules, and prioritize open work orders for the electrical team. Run shift operations when the primary supervisor is offsite.
• Perform maintenance, inspections, and troubleshooting on critical power systems, including backup generators, UPS systems, switchgear, transformers, and PDUs.
• Review methods of procedure (MOPs) and safety checklists before work begins. Confirm switching steps are clear, risks are identified, and backup power paths are verified.
• Lead daily pre-job safety briefings. Enforce LOTO protocols and NFPA 70E standards, and make sure the crew consistently wears proper arc-flash protection and PPE.
• Escort and monitor outside contractors and vendors performing specialized service or testing. Verify their work meets quality standards and facility rules.
• Keep accurate records of completed tasks, equipment run hours, and spare parts in the CMMS. Make sure inspection logs and test reports are properly filed.
• Train and mentor junior technicians on maintenance tasks, diagnostic tools, and safe work habits through consistent day-to-day coaching.
• Respond immediately to power alarms and system interruptions during shifts and on-call rotations. Assist with emergency recovery to protect the critical data center load.
• Other duties may be assigned.

What you’ll have

• Completion of an electrical apprenticeship, an associate degree in an electrical trade, or equivalent practical experience.
• At least 4 years of commercial or industrial electrical maintenance experience, including at least 1 year serving as a lead technician or crew chief.
• Solid understanding of electrical power distribution equipment, including switchgear, generators, transfer switches, and UPS systems.
• Demonstrated ability to read and interpret electrical one-line diagrams, schematics, and technical manuals.
• Strong practical knowledge of electrical safety rules, arc-flash hazards, and lockout/tagout procedures.
• Clear communication skills and the ability to coordinate tasks smoothly across maintenance and operations teams.

Physical requirements and work environment

• Ability to stand, walk, and perform repetitive tasks for extended periods

• Ability to lift and move equipment as needed (50 pounds)

• Ability to work onsite in a mining or data center environment (heat, noise, etc.)

jobs.title: Business Systems Analyst
jobs.description:
Proconex is the exclusive Emerson Impact Partner for Emerson Automation Solutions in the Mid-Atlantic region. We provide a full portfolio of Process Automation Control Systems, Valves and Control Devices, and related technologies and services to a range of customers—in the Life Sciences, Chemical, Power, Refining, Oil & Gas, Food & Beverage, Paper, Metals, and other industries, as well as commercial enterprises and campus facilities. With three strategically located offices, Proconex maintains a deep dedication to its 200+ employees, a sharp focus on safety and quality, and the drive to deliver.

Business Systems Analyst

Job Overview

The Business Systems Analyst serves as the bridge between business operations and technology, driving process improvement, system optimization, reporting, and digital transformation initiatives across the organization. This role partners with stakeholders throughout the company to understand operational challenges, identify opportunities for improvement, and deliver scalable technology solutions that improve efficiency, visibility, and decision-making.

The Business Systems Analyst will work extensively with ERP systems, business process automation, analytics platforms, reporting tools, and emerging AI technologies to support organizational goals. Success in this role requires strong analytical skills, business acumen, technical aptitude, and the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

This position supports process analysis, systems optimization, reporting, automation, and technology adoption efforts across the organization while serving as a key liaison between business stakeholders and technology resources.

Key Responsibilities

Business Process Improvement

• Analyze existing business processes, workflows, and operational procedures.

• Identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and areas for automation.

• Facilitate process improvement initiatives across departments.

• Document current-state and future-state workflows.

• Recommend solutions that improve efficiency, data quality, user experience, and business visibility.

• Identify and implement opportunities for operational improvement through continuous improvement initiatives.

Business Systems Administration & Optimization

• Partner with business teams to enhance and optimize enterprise applications.

• Support ERP configuration, testing, implementation, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Gather and document business requirements for system enhancements.

• Assist with user acceptance testing (UAT), issue resolution, and change management activities.

• Ensure business systems align with organizational objectives and industry best practices.

• Support user adoption and utilization of business systems through training, communication, and support.

Data & Analytics

• Develop dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using approved analytics tools.

• Translate business questions into meaningful metrics and reporting solutions.

• Analyze datasets to identify trends, opportunities, and performance insights.

• Promote data governance and reporting standards.

• Support self-service analytics adoption across the organization.

• Deliver reporting and business intelligence solutions that improve organizational visibility and decision-making.

Automation & Digital Transformation

• Identify opportunities to automate manual processes using modern technology platforms.

• Support workflow automation initiatives and business application integrations.

• Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI-enabled solutions, and recommend practical business applications.

• Participate in digital transformation projects from concept through implementation.

• Support the reduction of manual effort and improvement of operational scalability through technology-enabled solutions.

Stakeholder Engagement

• Serve as a liaison and partner to business leaders and subject matter experts.

• Facilitate discovery sessions and requirements-gathering workshops.

• Communicate project status, recommendations, risks, and business impacts to stakeholders.

• Provide user training, documentation, and adoption support for new solutions.

• Develop and maintain cross-functional relationships that support project delivery and organizational change.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Business, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in business analysis, business systems, process improvement, analytics, or related roles.

• 3+ years of experience gathering requirements and translating business needs into technical solutions.

• 3+ years of experience applying analytical and problem-solving skills in a business environment.

• 2+ years of experience utilizing written and verbal communication skills in a professional setting.

• 2+ years of experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with ERP platforms (IFS, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, or similar).

• Experience with Power BI or comparable analytics tools.

• Experience with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, Power Platform, SSMS, SSIS, and SSRS.

• Knowledge of SQL and relational databases.

• Experience with workflow automation platforms.

• Exposure to AI-powered business solutions and digital transformation initiatives.

• Experience supporting change management, user adoption, and business process transformation efforts.

jobs.title: Territory Manager, SUD (FL, West Palm Beach)
jobs.description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is one of the fastest-growing startups in the healthcare industry, working tirelessly to connect people everywhere to life-saving mental health and substance use treatment.

As an Territory Manager, SUD, you will join a founding go-to-market team responsible for scaling Charlie Health’s Substance Use Disorder (SUD) program nationally. SUD represents our next major growth vertical, and this team is charged with building the playbook.

You will play a direct role in shaping how we engage referral partners in key SUD settings such as detox centers, residential treatment centers, rehabilitation facilities, and other SUD-focused organizations. You will educate these partners about Charlie Health’s comprehensive SUD treatment and mental health programs, ensuring they understand how our services can support individuals on the path to recovery.

This role is best suited for someone who thrives in high-accountability environments and wants to help build something meaningful from the ground up. In your role, you’ll have unparalleled responsibility while collaborating with sharp, spirited, and ambitious coworkers. You’ll also receive competitive benefits, ensuring you have the resources to thrive both personally and professionally.

At Charlie Health, we believe in leading with our “why” and connecting with our purpose every day. Join us to find not only a career but a calling.

Responsibilities

• Develop and execute a territory-level go-to-market strategy focused on growing our SUD program

• Build deep, trust-based relationships with higher and lower level of care SUD referral partners

• Conduct in-field outreach 4-5 days per week, meeting with referral partners to educate them about Charlie Health’s SUD programs and services

• Identify barriers to treatment and collaborate with referral sources to improve access to care for individuals in need

• Collect and synthesize partner feedback to refine messaging, positioning, and execution.

• Collaborate with leadership and cross-functional teams to continuously improve the SUD growth motion.

• Partner with internal teams to create tailored engagement strategies that resonate with SUD care providers and support long-term collaboration

• Represent Charlie Health in both community settings as well as industry events, conferences, and educational sessions to promote awareness of our SUD program

• Gather and synthesize feedback from partners and stakeholders to refine marketing, operational, and product strategies

• Work cross-functionally with marketing, clinical, operations, and analytics teams to achieve growth goals within the SUD channel

Requirements

• Must be based in West Palm Beach, FL

• Willingness to travel extensively around West Palm Beach, FL

• 4+ years of proven sales or business development experience

• Experience in healthcare or behavioral health outreach preferred

• Familiarity with the SUD treatment ecosystem and community ties preferred

• Demonstrated ability to build relationships, educate stakeholders, and foster collaboration

• Exceptional interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills

• Strong project management skills, with a knack for managing details in a dynamic environment

• Experience with Microsoft Office, Teams, and Salesforce is a plus

Benefits

Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Additional Information

The total target base compensation for this role will be between $70,000 and $90,000 per year at the commencement of employment. In addition to base compensation, this role offers an uncapped performance-based bonus with overall expected compensation will be between $94,000 and $114,000. Please note, pay will be determined on an individualized basis and will be impacted by location, experience, expertise, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations.

Our Values

• Connection: Care deeply & inspire hope.

jobs.description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

Overview

ADAS DRE - Sensors is responsible for managing the release process for our camera systems. This role bridges hardware release, systems engineering, and cross-functional coordination to ensure successful integration of all camera systems into Scout vehicles. The role owns assigned camera hardware and mounting-system deliverables through integration, validation, issue resolution, and release, applying independent judgment within established engineering processes and escalating issues that exceed the role’s authority.

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

• Own the hardware release of assigned camera system components, including associated mounting brackets, and ensure release deliverables meet defined technical, quality, timing, and documentation requirements.

• Lead the integration of assigned camera system components into the Scout architecture while meeting installation guidelines and component performance requirements.

• Collaborate with multidisciplinary and multicultural teams, including electrical engineers, software developers, and validation engineers, to define system requirements, evaluate technical tradeoffs, and ensure camera system performance.

• Plan and execute system-level testing, validation, and verification activities for assigned sensor components, including real-world testing and data analysis, to validate system performance and compliance with applicable regulatory standards.

• Act as the single point of contact for assigned camera hardware and mounting systems within Scout; evaluate identifiable technical factors, recommend the appropriate course of action, and lead component issue tracking and resolution plans through closure.

• Adapt existing engineering approaches and precedents to address unusual circumstances, and escalate decisions or risks that exceed the role’s assigned scope or authority.

• Communicate technical status, risks, recommendations, and resolution plans to cross-functional partners and senior contacts, adapting the level of detail to the audience.

• Stay up-to-date with the latest advancements in ADAS technologies, industry trends, and regulatory requirements to drive continuous improvement.

• Be Scout’s innovator for new solutions that excite our customers!

• This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.

• Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

What you’ll bring

You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:
