jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Veza

Veza is the identity security platform for human, non-human, and AI agent access. Customers use it to see who and what has access to what, govern it, and remediate risk across cloud, SaaS, and on-prem systems.

Agent security is the inflection point. Static access reviews can't keep up with autonomous agents acting at machine speed. Security is shifting to continuous, real-time control: just-in-time access for agents, automated remediation of policy violations, and real-time governance of agent actions as they happen—replacing standing privileges and periodic reviews.

Veza is in transition, growing quickly as part of ServiceNow's Security & Risk organization. The Chief Architect will shape how the platform scales to meet this new category.

What you'll do

• Own the end-to-end architecture of the Veza platform, including the access graph, ingestion pipeline, authorization and policy engine, and the services built on them. Lead the evolution toward a graph-native data model (Neo4j or equivalent) that scales to billions of relationships and complex permission hierarchies. Set the standards every team builds to.
• Lead the next-generation data architecture. Evolve the core graph and storage model for order-of-magnitude growth in customers, entities, and relationships, with a clear migration path from today's system and no customer disruption.
• Define the architecture for non-human identity and AI agent security. Make Veza the system of record for what agents can access, and design for governance, guardrails, and auditability.
• Set the AI architecture for Veza's own agents and features: agentic patterns, evaluation, observability, cost and capacity planning, and a multi-vendor LLM strategy that avoids lock-in.
• Modernize the integrations framework. Veza has 300+ integrations, and they drive a disproportionate share of support load. Establish a scalable, testable, self-service framework that raises reliability and cuts onboarding time.
• Architect how Veza fits into ServiceNow. Veza is not built on the ServiceNow platform. Define the integration model, shared identity and data contracts, and UI surfacing patterns that deliver a unified customer experience without forcing a rewrite.
• Drive deployment flexibility: multi-region SaaS, data residency, regulated-industry requirements (e.g., EU financial regulation such as DORA), and federal-grade deployment, including the compliance and operational constraints each brings.
• Govern architecture across teams. Run architecture reviews, manage tech debt and the security backlog, and make clear, documented build-vs-buy and sequencing decisions.
• Raise the bar on engineering practice, including heavy use of AI coding agents, automated testing coverage, defect escape reduction, and operational excellence with SRE.
• Represent Veza's architecture to executives, customers, partners, and ServiceNow architecture and security leadership.
• Mentor architects and senior engineers and build the next layer of technical leadership.

What you bring

Core

• 15+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years as a staff/principal/chief architect, or equivalent, over a large multi-team platform.
• Deep experience designing multi-tenant, cloud-native SaaS at enterprise scale: distributed systems, large-scale data and graph systems, APIs, and microservices.
• Hands-on Kubernetes and cloud experience (AWS required; multi-cloud a plus) and modern DevOps, IaC, and SRE practices.
• Strong background in graph databases and data structures. Hands-on experience with Neo4j, or similar graph platforms; understanding of immutable or event-sourced storage models and their operational trade-offs.
• A track record of leading large architectural migrations in a live production system.
• Experience influencing without direct authority across multiple teams and geographies (US, EU, India).
• Executive-level communication, with the ability to write and defend an architecture decision to engineers, customers, and the C-suite.
• Strong proficiency in Python and Go or Java, with the ability to go deep in code and design reviews.

Security and identity

• Strong background in identity and access: IGA, IAM, PAM, authorization models, access reviews, lifecycle management, or adjacent security domains.
• Understanding of non-human identity (service accounts, secrets, API keys, workload identity) and emerging agent identity and authorization models.
• Experience building security products that meet their own security and compliance bar (SOC 2, FedRAMP or equivalent, data residency).

AI

• Experience delivering production AI systems: LLMs, agentic architectures, RAG, evaluation, observability, guardrails, human-in-the-loop, and managing model cost and capacity.
• Active use of AI-native development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent) and the ability to drive adoption across teams.

Preferred

• Experience through an acquisition or platform integration, aligning an acquired architecture with a parent platform.
• Prior experience with integration-heavy platforms (hundreds of connectors) and the reliability challenges they bring.
• Familiarity with graph databases or immutable/event-sourced storage models.
• BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Success in the first 12 months

• A published, org-wide architecture vision and roadmap for the next-generation platform, with committed milestones.
• An integrations modernization plan in flight, with measurable reduction in escalations and onboarding time.
• A defined, adopted pattern for Veza-ServiceNow integration and UI surfacing.
• A sustainable architecture review and governance process the teams actually use.
• Clear architecture for agent and NHI security that product and sales can take to customers.

Become part of something big with Extreme! As a global networking leader, learn why there is no better time to join the Extreme team.

Position type: Full time - Hybrid
Location:  Seattle, WA

Application deadline: Applications are being accepted on a rolling basis and this posting will remain open until filled.

Scope:
Are you energized by solving complex, high-impact problems directly with customers? Do you want to turn emerging technologies in intelligent networking, generative AI, agentic systems, automation, and cloud platforms into production solutions? Forward Deployed Engineers at Extreme are software engineers who work directly with strategic customers to jointly design, build, validate, and deploy solutions to complex business and technical problems using Extreme's products and platforms.
FDEs operate in real customer environments and own technical outcomes from discovery and solution design through implementation, deployment, and production readiness. FDEs also identify platform gaps and define new feature requirements, working with Product teams to incorporate recurring customer needs into Extreme's products and platforms.

As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, you will be the technical lead for complex customer engagements, owning solutions from discovery and architecture through implementation, deployment, and production readiness.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
Hyliion is committed to creating innovative solutions that enable clean, flexible and affordable electricity production. The Company’s primary focus is to develop distributed power generators that can operate on various fuel sources to future-proof against an ever-changing energy economy.

Job Purpose

The Manufacturing Engineer designs, implements, and improves assembly processes and equipment within the Industrialization team. This position develops the assembly lines, fixtures, and material flow systems that convert KARNO prototype and development builds into repeatable, scalable production operations — and then works to remove waste, labor content, and variation from those operations.

Working closely with industrialization leadership, design engineering, production, quality, and supply chain, the Manufacturing Engineer owns assigned assembly processes and stations: line and station design, fixture and tooling design, material presentation and handling, process qualification, and continuous waste reduction. This position applies Hyliion’s standards for how assembly processes are designed and documented, participates in design reviews, and contributes to measurable improvement in cycle time, first-pass yield, labor content, and ergonomics across the assembly areas.

AI at Hyliion

At Hyliion, AI is core to how we work. We equip every team member with leading AI tools and count on you to use them — to move faster, solve harder problems, and help us realize the full potential of KARNO technology for the world.

Duties and Responsibilities

• Assembly Line and Cell Design: Design and improve assembly lines, cells, and workstations for KARNO core, module, and subassembly operations. Establish work sequencing, balance work content to takt, define station layouts and footprints, and design lines that accommodate planned rate increases rather than requiring rebuild to reach them.

• Fixture, Jig, and Tooling Design: Design assembly and inspection fixtures, jigs, and tooling from concept through qualification. Own datum and locating strategy, tolerance stack-up and GD&T, error-proofing (poka-yoke) features, and fixture qualification including repeatability and gage R&R studies. Participate in peer design reviews of fixtures and tooling.

• Material Handling and Flow Optimization: Design material presentation and handling systems that put the right part at the point of use in the right orientation — kitting strategy, cart and rack design, sequencing, kanban and pull loops, and travel distance and motion reduction. Partner with Supply Chain and Production Control on line-side stocking, min/max levels, and WIP control.

• Waste Reduction in Assembly Operations: Systematically identify and eliminate waste across assembly operations — motion, waiting, rework, overprocessing, transport, and excess inventory. Reduce labor content and cycle time per unit through standard work, work sequencing, changeover reduction, error-proofing, and station design. Quantify the value of each change before implementation and verify the result afterward.

• Prototype Development and Production Scaling: Collaborate with design engineering to develop prototype build processes and transition them to efficient, repeatable production-scale operations, including cross-site process transfer between the Milford, OH and Cedar Park, TX facilities.

• Process Development and Optimization: Design, develop, implement, and qualify manufacturing processes for engine, generator, electric machine, and precision electromechanical assembly operations, including processes involving high-voltage systems, sealed pressure systems, and additively manufactured components.

• Process Documentation and Control: Author and maintain the process documentation set — PFMEAs, control plans, work instructions, travelers, and routings — and ensure the manufacturing BOM structure reflects how the product is actually built. Verify on the floor that the documented process is the process being followed.

• Technical Collaboration and Support: Provide technical guidance to production teams and technicians on assigned processes, participate in design reviews, and represent Manufacturing Engineering on assigned projects to influence design for manufacturability.

• Capital Equipment and Automation: Support the specification, justification, procurement, installation, and qualification of capital equipment, semi-automated assembly aids, and material handling equipment. Contribute to business cases and vendor evaluations, and own installation and process qualification for assigned equipment through to validated production use.

• Additive Manufacturing: Integrate additive manufacturing technologies into production processes where applicable, including design and process considerations specific to additively manufactured assemblies.

• Problem-Solving and Root Cause Analysis: Lead or support root cause analysis and corrective action for assembly process and quality issues using 5-Why, 8D, DOE, and statistical methods. Drive corrective actions to verified closure rather than disposition.

• Project Management: Manage assigned industrialization projects and workstreams, ensuring timelines, budgets, and objectives are met, and escalating early with a recommendation attached.

• Safety and Ergonomics: Design workstations, fixtures, and material handling that support safe work — reach, lift, posture, tool access, and energy control. Participate actively in hazard identification, near-miss reporting, and LOTO and electrical safety discipline.

• Additional duties and responsibilities as assigned, needed, or required for the business.

Qualifications

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Qualifications include:

• Education, Experience and Certifications Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, or Industrial Engineering (or related field) required. 3–5 years of experience in a manufacturing engineering role, preferably with exposure to engine, genset, electric motor, or precision electromechanical assembly operations. Hands-on experience contributing to assembly line and cell design, from concept layout through installed and qualified production use. Hands-on experience in fixture, jig, and tooling design — designing, building, and qualifying fixtures, not only specifying them. Experience taking prototype and low-volume builds into repeatable production processes. Familiarity with business case drivers and value creation. Ability to objectively compare and rationalize options for the path forward. Aerospace or other precision manufacturing industry experience is preferred. Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt) beneficial.

• Skills and Abilities Solid working knowledge of assembly process and equipment design: line layout and balancing, station and workstation design, fixture and tooling design, error-proofing, and process qualification. Proficiency in 3D CAD required, with Siemens NX strongly preferred — NX is our design platform, and native fluency accelerates contribution meaningfully. Candidates with strong proficiency in another major platform (SolidWorks, CATIA, Creo, Inventor, or equivalent) will receive full consideration and are expected to develop working NX proficiency within the first several months; demonstrated willingness and aptitude to learn NX is required. Fluency in tolerance stack-up analysis and GD&T, and the ability to read, interpret, and challenge engineering drawings, BOMs, ECOs, and specifications. Demonstrated skill in material handling and flow design — point-of-use presentation, kitting, kanban and pull systems, line-side stocking, and travel distance and motion reduction. Practical experience with waste identification and elimination in assembly operations, including time study and work measurement, standard work development, changeover reduction, and labor content analysis. Working knowledge of DOE, gage R&R, capability studies, and formal process qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ or equivalent). Exposure to implementing automation and semi-automated assembly aids into production processes. Experience with one or more of the following: custom fabrication, engine and generator assembly, and electric motor or electric machine assembly processes. Proficiency with manufacturing execution systems (MES) and ERP routing and BOM structures; PLM experience (Teamcenter or equivalent) beneficial. Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement methodologies applied in practice rather than in theory. Familiarity with automotive or aerospace industry standards and regulatory requirements (e.g., QS9000, ISO 9001, AS9100, NADCAP). Experience with additive manufacturing (3D printing) beneficial. Ability to collaborate effectively with engineers, technicians, and cross-functional partners, contribute to design reviews, and influence without direct authority. Comfort operating in a pre-commercial environment where product configuration is still changing and the process must be built rather than inherited.

Role Classification and Working Conditions

This is a salaried, exempt-level position. This position typically works in an office environment; and given the nature of our business is also exposed to operations/warehouses/production environments.

Physical/Other Requirements

• Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, access equipment in confined or elevated positions, and occasionally lift and move materials up to 40 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• Compliance with all site PPE and safety requirements is mandatory.

• Temporary extended on-site oversight for new process development preferred.

• Ongoing travel to company engineering and production sites up to 30%.

We are not accepting candidates who require sponsorship for this role at this time.

jobs.title: Principal Chemist
jobs.description:
Principal Oligonucleotide Chemist

Company: LGC Biosearch Technologies

Location: 2100 South McDowell, Petaluma, CA 94952

Type: Full‑time

Company Overview

LGC Biosearch Technologies operates across manufacturing sites in the US, UK, Germany, and Denmark, providing mission‑critical genomics solutions to customers in molecular diagnostics, pharma/biotech, and agrigenomics. Our integrated portfolio of products, services, and expertise supports our mission of Science for a Safer World. We partner closely with customers to enable research and development of life‑altering treatments for diseases worldwide. Join our high‑growth, purpose‑driven organization.

Position Summary

The Principal Oligonucleotide Chemist is a senior scientific leader responsible for driving oligonucleotide product development, synthesis, process development, and innovation across the Innovation Hub, operations, and customer‑facing programs. This role blends hands‑on laboratory execution with strategic experimental design, data‑driven development, project leadership, and mentorship of scientists to deliver new products.

You will serve as the technical lead for Oligonucleotide New Product Development (NPD), and Customer co‑creation product projects, designing new manufacturing methods, troubleshooting complex issues, supporting tech transfer, and presenting technical content to commercial teams and customers. This position plays a critical role in advancing LGC’s oligonucleotide chemistry capabilities and new product offerings.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership in Oligonucleotide Chemistry, Project Execution and Delivery

• Lead Petaluma Innovation Hub Oligo Chemistry Function by delivering customer co‑creation and NPD products/projects from concept through delivery.
• Partner with peers and global team to deliver to customers and achieve Innovation Hub development and financial objectives.
• Serve as a technical lead for multi-site, multi-function development team for oligonucleotide synthesis, modification, deprotection, purification, and analytical characterization.
• Participate in evaluation of new technologies and oligonucleotide market strategy
• Oversee and Execute oligo synthesis projects, including experimental design/planning, prioritization, and resource coordination.
• Deliver and control new methods, workflows, and manufacturing protocols for oligonucleotide synthesis, purification and analysis. Support operations technically.
• Optimize, and define manufacturing instructions for low‑yielding or impure processes.

Laboratory Execution & Product Manufacturing

• Lead projects and staff hands-on in the lab by performing and training synthesis and purification of oligonucleotides using automated and manual techniques.
• Conduct analytical characterization (LC‑MS, HPLC, CE, UV‑Vis) to confirm identity, purity, and impurity profiles.
• Troubleshoot synthetic routes, instrument performance, and purification workflows and analytics to ensure consistent, high‑quality output.
• Develop and refine synthetic routes, synthesis method refinement, coupling conditions, deprotection strategies and purification methods.

Experimental Design, Data Analysis & Development Strategy

• Design rigorous, data‑driven experiments to optimize yield, purity, scalability (up and down), and process robustness.
• Use mechanistic understanding and statistical analysis to adjust development plans and guide next‑step decision‑making.
• Lead troubleshooting efforts by designing investigation maps and structured experimental plans.
• Document experimental results, conclusions, and recommendations by industry standard technical summary reports and within quality certification requirements.

Customer Co‑Creation & Technical Communication

• Successfully lead and deliver oligonucleotide customer co‑creation and NPD projects.
• Participate in technical customer calls related to custom oligo manufacturing, product investigations, and development updates.
• Present technical content to commercial teams and customers, including data reviews, capability overviews, and project progress.

Operations Support, Tech Transfer & Continuous Improvement

• Provide technical support to Operations for process optimization, scale‑up, and continual improvement.
• Lead the successful transfer of custom product methods and procedures into MSAT and Operations teams.Develop effective tech transfer plans and verify training for newly developed processes.Deliver method validation in alignment with Quality department requirements.
• Support troubleshooting and root‑cause investigations for manufacturing challenges.

Mentorship & Team Development

• Mentor and develop scientists in oligonucleotide chemistry; providing guidance in technical skills, experimental design, and professional development.
• Promote rigorous laboratory order and management, controlled documentation, and best practices in experimental execution.
• Foster a collaborative, trust building and growth‑oriented environment that supports scientific excellence.

Technical Skills

• Proven expertise in oligonucleotide chemistry.
• Demonstrated knowledge of solid‑phase oligonucleotide synthesis and modification.
• Skilled in analytical characterization of oligonucleotides, including impurity profiling.
• Demonstrated project management skills with experience leading matrixed teams through complex development projects.

Seasoned ability to design, optimize, and troubleshoot oligonucleotide manufacturing development processes

Qualifications

• Ph.D. in Synthetic Organic Chemistry, Chemical Biology, or related field inclusive of extensive experience in oligonucleotide chemistry.
• Minimum of 15 years of direct industry experience in oligonucleotide synthesis, product and process development, and tech transfer into manufacturing.
• Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects, mentor scientists, and collaborate cross‑functionally.
• Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical content to internal and external audiences.

Minimum: $ 131,155/ Annualy

Maximum: $196,733/ Anually

This range represents the low and high end of the anticipated salary range for the California -based position.  The actual base salary will depend on several factors such as: experience, skills, and location.

LGC is a leading, global life science tools company, providing mission-critical components and solutions into high-growth application areas across the human healthcare and applied market segments. Its high-quality product portfolio is comprised of mission-critical tools for genomic analysis and for quality assurance applications, which are typically embedded and recurring within our customers’ products and workflows and are valued for their performance, quality, and range.

jobs.title: Major Account Director
jobs.description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster.

Proudly based in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we’ve raised a $72M Series C, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (Fast 500™), signed multi-year AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier, and grown to a team of 250+.

About the role

In your role as Major Account Director, you will play a critical role in the growth and expansion of existing CoLab customers. You will work with current enterprise customer accounts to achieve business outcomes with industry-relevant solutions. In this role, you build and execute strategies to help land and expand 7-figure accounts. The ideal person for this role is passionate about helping others succeed and cultivating strong relationships.

This position will require occasional travel for on-site team meetings in Newfoundland Canada, at least twice per year (primarily in December and June) in addition to occasional travel to off sites. We recognize that travel can involve personal commitments, and we strive to accommodate individual circumstances, however the expectation is that travel to, and attendance at, the majority of these events is mandatory. Details about travel arrangements and covered expenses will be discussed during the hiring process.

What you’ll do:

• Build relationships with existing customers and net new strategic accounts.

• Build and execute a robust account strategy and plan to help the customer get the most value possible and CoLab to drive significant revenue growth. This includes deep account planning, mapping and multi-threaded selling.

• Serve as an expert to your customers as it relates to CoLab and industry best practices.

• Find, qualify and build opportunities within existing accounts.

• Work in consultation with Account Executive and Customer Success teams enterprise account expansions and renewals.

• Help drive growth among our customers by understanding their business and technical needs in order to achieve their desired outcomes.

• Manage follow-up conversations and document all activities in Salesforce.

• Travel to customer on-site on average 1 week per month.

Who you are:

• Experience managing complex enterprise or major accounts within a SaaS business, or an engineering background paired with strong closing skills.

• Experience working with large enterprise customers for at least 1-2 years (10,000 employees +)

• Ability to understand and analyze use cases and demonstrate highly technical product.

• A strategic thinker with the ability to navigate complex enterprise sales for a product that is new to market.

• Comfortable with complex account planning and account mapping and selling across multiple departments.

• Committed team player with an ownership mindset and no ego.

• Deeply passionate and self-motivated to achieve goals and results.

• Resilient - challenges excited you and you’re not afraid to overcome roadblocks.

• Excellent communication skills and ability to convey your message.

• Excited to work in a fast-moving startup environment with a lot of change.

• Bonus: have worked with manufacturing clients (including but not limited to automotive, medical device and hardware/mechanical consumer products).

Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups often apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. At CoLab, we believe in potential over perfection. If this role excites you—even if you don’t meet every single qualification—we encourage you to apply. Your unique background and perspective are valuable to us.

jobs.title: Member Experience (New Grad)
jobs.description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As part of our Member Experience team, you will play a vital role in delivering unparalleled support, working directly with customers to provide a world-class experience. You will be the voice and advocate of our brand, ensuring every interaction leaves a lasting impression of trust, satisfaction, and delight. By actively addressing customer needs and exceeding their expectations, you will contribute not only to the success of our customers but also to the growth and reputation of our company. This role offers a unique opportunity to develop real-world expertise in customer service, creative problem-solving, and impactful communication, all while making a tangible difference in the lives of our customers and the future of Base. 

 

What You'll Do

 - Engage with members across phone, email, text, and other communication channels, delivering personalized and delightful experiences that leave a lasting impact.

 - Troubleshoot and resolve member issues related to Base Power's innovative products, ensuring seamless and satisfying solutions.

 - Utilize tools to track, manage, troubleshoot, and prioritize member interactions, ensuring every concern is addressed promptly and efficiently.

 - Partner with engineering, marketing, and operations teams to streamline processes, enhance the member experience, and drive continuous improvement.

 - Act as the “voice of the customer”, gathering valuable feedback and insights to shape the future of our products and services.

 - Create and maintain detailed documentation, knowledge bases, playbooks, and team resources to ensure consistency in service.

 - Support new members during onboarding to ensure they understand and can fully utilize Base Power's products from the start.
   
    

What You'll Bring

 - Graduation year between 2025-2027.

 - Empathetic communicator who loves connecting with people and making them feel heard.

 - Strong writing skills with excellent grammar, tone, and clarity.

 - Ability to think analytically and creatively to resolve complex issues and suggest process improvements.

 - Attention to detail in communicating accurately and clearly, tracking customer interactions, and documenting solutions.

 - Skilled at managing multiple tasks and inquiries simultaneously while meeting deadlines and response time goals.

 - Natural inclination to stay calm under pressure and step up to proactively de-escalate frustrating situations.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-paced environment to quickly adapt to changes while maintaining high-quality support.

 - Tech savvy, with a knack for quickly mastering new tools and systems.

 - Team player motivated by the mission who always puts the company’s best interests first.

 

About the Team

The Member Experience team is the face of Base to our members—and the voice of our members back to Base. We’re deeply customer-obsessed and uniquely cross-functional, with a strong understanding of what every team does and how it all connects. By seeing firsthand what’s working well and what should be improved, we surface insights that help inform what the business builds and prioritizes next. Every day brings a new challenge, balancing high ownership and accountability with constant collaboration and support from the team.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Structuring (Tax/Preferred Equity)
jobs.description:
WE’RE FINANCING THE FUTURE OF ENERGY

Crux is the capital platform for the clean economy. We modernize capital raising and deployment for clean energy and critical infrastructure with solutions across advisory, investments, technology, and intelligence.

Our team of 120+ is composed of experts in energy, tax, finance, government, and technology. We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Overture, Ardent Venture Partners, QED, Canapi, and others. These funds are joined by strategic investors including Pattern Energy, Clearway Energy, EDF Renewables, Intersect Power, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.

 


AN INFLECTION POINT IN AMERICAN ENERGY AND MANUFACTURING

Energy demand is growing for the first time in decades, driving an urgent need for more affordable and reliable electricity. More electricity requires new clean energy infrastructure and strong domestic supply chains for minerals and components — as well as large amounts of capital.

Traditional project financing is opaque, fragmented, and analog. At Crux, we’re changing that. Through unmatched insights and expertise, white-glove service, purpose-built tools, and risk underwriting, we power a more prosperous, clean, and secure energy future.

We are scaling quickly and looking for team members who are eager to combine deep expertise with an AI-and tech-forward mindset. 

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Manager, Tax/Preferred Equity will be a core member of Crux’s Structuring team, reporting to leadership within the Structuring team. The team delivers capital solutions across tax equity, preferred equity, debt, and advisory services to sponsors, developers, and investors. This role sits on the tax/preferred equity side of the team and is a hands-on execution role for an experienced structuring professional with a strong working knowledge of these structures, covering project-level and portfolio-level transactions in renewable energy and energy transition infrastructure. The Senior Manager will be responsible for leading screening and underwriting, building, maintaining, and stress-testing tax/preferred equity models, preparing investment analyses for internal and external stakeholders, and driving transaction execution from intake to closing, while helping to guide and develop Associates on the team.

This position is ideal for candidates with at least 4 years of relevant experience in structured finance, renewable energy, infrastructure investing, or a closely related field, particularly those with meaningful exposure to structuring partnership flip, hybrid, and preferred equity transactions, including building the underlying models. Candidates should be comfortable leading transaction workstreams, working across teams, adopting new tools and AI-enabled workflows, and engaging directly with clients.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build, maintain, and audit complex financial models for tax/hybrid and preferred equity transactions, with a focus on partnership flip, T-flip, and hybrid structures (experience with other parts of the capital stack a plus).

 - Lead the screening and underwriting of new opportunities, including initial reviews and pre-pricing screens, and develop pricing and structuring recommendations.

 - Lead the preparation of investment materials for Investment Committee, including transaction economics, sensitivities, and risk analyses.

 - Collaborate with senior members of the Structuring team on transaction structuring, execution, and negotiations, driving transactions from intake to closing.

 - Analyze sponsor financials, project contracts, and diligence materials to identify risks and value drivers.

 - Coordinate diligence across commercial, technical, legal, tax, and insurance workstreams (independent engineer, tax opinions, appraisals, tax insurance), and review transaction documents including term sheets, LLC agreements, equity capital contribution agreements, and closing checklists.

 - Leverage technology and AI-enabled tools to increase accuracy and efficiency in modeling, diligence, and reporting.

 - Contribute to process improvements and template standardization (models, IC memos, term sheets) across the Structuring team.

 - Engage directly with developers, investors, and advisors on active transactions, taking increasing ownership of counterparty relationships.

 - Review the work of and help develop Associates on the Structuring team.

 - Support platform initiatives to scale tax/preferred equity workflows and develop new tech-enabled products and solutions for financing processes.

 - Support portfolio management and reporting as needed, including monitoring project performance against underwriting.
   
    


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, or a related field; MBA or MS a plus.

 - Minimum 4+ years of experience in renewable energy, structured finance, infrastructure investing, investment banking, or a closely related field, with direct tax equity and/or preferred equity structuring and modeling experience required.

 - Advanced Excel skills, including the ability to build complex partnership models from scratch; VBA or Python skills a plus.

 - Strong understanding of tax equity and preferred equity structures (partnership flip, hybrid, preferred equity; sale-leaseback optional), including allocations, capital accounts, and flip mechanics.

 - Experience leading transaction workstreams, preparing transaction materials, and coordinating due diligence (independent engineer, tax opinions, appraisals, tax insurance).

 - Familiarity with IRS requirements, safe harbor tests, and recapture provisions preferred.

 - Experience in a transaction-focused environment with direct client interaction responsibility.

 - Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with proven ability to manage multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

 - Comfortable adopting new technology platforms and integrating AI tools into daily workflows.

 - FINRA SIE, Series 79, and 63, or willingness to obtain them under Crux’s broker-dealer sponsorship.
   
    


WHAT WE BRING

 - Backing, traction & brand:
   
   - We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Ardent Venture Partners, Pattern, Clearway, EDFR, Intersect, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.
   
   - $500m debt warehouse facility from Nuveen to invest in clean energy.
   
   - Have been profitable and are growing exponentially
   
   - We have closed over 120+ transactions in just the last 2 years, facilitating billions of dollars of capital flowing into renewables projects

 - Culture & working dynamic
   
   - Remote-first operating model: Work from anywhere in the US and Canada, or work out of our optional offices in DC, NYC, & SF. Optional co-working opportunities with co-workers in, Seattle, Denver, Boston, LA, and beyond.
   
   - High growth & high ownership culture: We grow quickly by giving extremely talented people a lot of responsibility.
   
   - Best of financial services & technology: We have brought together a team that are experts in clean energy finance, and the best technologies. Use your expertise while getting to be on the cutting edge of applying AI to your day and your clients’ experience.
   
   - Regular team offsites: We sustain culture by bringing the entire company together 2 times a year. Individual teams may also meet up more frequently.

 - Benefits
   
   - Healthcare: We cover 100% of premiums for employees with a variety of plans on Aetna (nationwide) and Kaiser (WA and California) and subsidize 70% for dependents (total as a group), if relevant.
   
   - Dental & vision: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and 50% for dependents (each), if relevant.
   
   - Holidays: 10 company holidays per year.
   
   - Paid time off: 20 days per year.
   
   - 401k: We support a 401k account but don't have a matching program set up at this time (typical for an early-stage startup).
   
   - Parental leave: 16 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents.

 - Compensation:
   
   - Compensation: $200,000s - $300,000s, depending on years of exp. & revenue scope, not inclusive of equity value.
   
   - Stock options in a rapidly growing company.

 - Values
   
   - Care for each other: We want to work on a team where people support each other - in their growth, in their work, and towards our shared mission. When we do that, we have fun.
   
   - Build and improve rapidly: We move quickly. To do that, we focus, consistently ask ourselves if we are prioritizing the right things, and execute them as best as possible.
   
   - Focus unremittingly on customers: Our first obligation is to our customers and partners, and we keep their needs front and center in everything we do.
   
   - Demonstrate ownership: We are all owners of Crux. This is our team, our company, our product and we show that to each other.
   
   - Convene a team that reflects the breadth of experiences in the country: We’re building a team with a wide range of backgrounds and a culture where everyone can thrive.

We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by law.

As a liaison between customers and the technical team, the Product Support Manager will focus on enhancing customer experience, driving customer satisfaction, and supporting product improvements based on customer feedback.

Primary Responsibilities

• Lead, schedule, and develop a team of technicians supporting gas reciprocating engine power generation packages and related systems.

• Assign and prioritize equipment monitoring, inspections, preventive maintenance, corrective repairs, and installation and startup support based on operational and customer needs.

• Serve as the escalation point for complex technical issues, equipment shutdowns or trips, and customer concerns, coordinating timely resolution with technicians and other departments.

• Maintain current support procedures and technical documentation, and oversee the adoption of new tools and technologies that improve team effectiveness.

• Ensure the team follows all Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) policies, including required PPE, safety meetings, and safe work practices, particularly during urgent response situations.

• Maintain current knowledge of company products, services, and applicable equipment to support technicians and customers effectively.

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

• Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees

• Generous PTO + paid holidays

• 401(k) + company match

• Gym membership stipend + wellness programs (earn PTO and prizes!)

• Company events, food truck nights

• 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year — give back to the community you call home

• Career advancement, leadership training, and professional development opportunities

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

• See challenges as opportunities

• Embrace change and continuous improvement

• Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

Skills & Qualifications

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Familiarity with support software and technologies Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment Excellent communication and interpersonal skills Proactive and results-oriented mindset Experience with product management or development Proven leadership and team management skills Strong understanding of customer support processes and methodologies Excellent organizational and multitasking abilities Strong written and verbal communication skills Ability to analyze data and generate actionable insights Experience developing and implementing support strategies Customer-focused with a commitment to delivering exceptional service Education and Experience: High School Diploma or Equivalent Education or Experience required. At least 8+ years of experience in customer support or technical support role Previous experience in a managerial or supervisory position Physical Requirements: Must be able to lift at least 50 lbs Travel is expected approximately 40% of the time

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

jobs.title: Senior Hardware Engineer
jobs.description:
The Senior Hardware Engineer supports or owns the design of automotive computing products, including infotainment, connectivity, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), and cross-domain electronic control units. The role translates customer and market requirements into robust, cost-effective hardware designs and leads those designs through verification, validation, industrialization, and mass-production launch.

• Work directly with automotive OEM customers to elicit, analyze, document, and manage functional, electrical, environmental, safety, and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements.
• Define system and hardware architectures for products that include switch-mode power supplies, power switches, LVDS transceivers, HDMI receivers, USB hubs, embedded microcontrollers, audio/video codecs, and standards-based wireless communications such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
• Lead schematic design, component selection, design reviews, interface definition, and printed circuit board layout guidance, including signal-integrity, power-integrity, thermal, grounding, and design-for-manufacturing considerations.
• Perform simulations, worst-case circuit analysis, tolerance analysis, design failure mode and effects analyses (DFMEAs), fault-tree analyses, and similar design-assurance activities.
• Develop and negotiate hardware verification and EMC validation plans that satisfy internal, customer, and applicable automotive requirements; maintain requirements-to-test traceability.
• Troubleshoot validation, manufacturing, and vehicle issues through bench-level debugging, testing, measurement, root-cause analysis, and prototyping; drive corrective actions to closure.
• Manage hardware deliverables, technical risks, design documentation, change control, and release readiness across the product life cycle.
• Lead and collaborate with local and global cross-functional engineering teams, suppliers, manufacturing partners, and customers to meet quality, cost, timing, and performance targets.
• Mentor less-experienced engineers and contribute to hardware design standards, reusable methods, and continuous improvement.
• Travel as required, including occasional international travel and travel to domestic customer and global company locations.

Minimum:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, electronics engineering, computer engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline.
• 7 years of experience designing and developing electronic hardware, including ownership of complex circuit designs and delivery through verification or production release.
• Demonstrated proficiency in schematic capture, circuit analysis, laboratory debugging, technical documentation, and design reviews.
• Ability to communicate technical decisions clearly and collaborate effectively across disciplines, organizations, and geographic regions.

Preferred:

• Master’s degree in electrical engineering or a closely related discipline.
• Experience with automotive hardware-development practices, OEM customer requirements, product-quality processes, and applicable environmental, EMC, and electrical-transient standards.
• Full product-life-cycle experience with automotive electronics, including requirements, architecture and concept development, component selection, schematic design, analysis, simulation, verification, validation, industrialization, production launch, and sustaining engineering.
• Digital design experience with processors, microcontrollers, memories, display interfaces, I²S, I²C, SPI, and high-speed serial interfaces such as USB 2.0/3.x, Ethernet, PCI Express, and HDMI.
• Analog and mixed-signal design experience with audio, video, sensor interfaces, power supplies, power sequencing, and radio-frequency technologies such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
• Experience applying signal-integrity, power-integrity, electromagnetic interference (EMI), radio-frequency interference (RFI), electrostatic discharge (ESD), grounding, shielding, and thermal-design methods.
• Experience developing and executing design verification plans and reports (DVP&R), interpreting test results, and resolving nonconformities.
• Proficiency with current laboratory equipment, including oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, logic analyzers, electronic loads, power analyzers, and environmental or EMC test equipment.
• Experience with circuit-simulation, schematic-capture, PCB-layout, requirements-management, and product-life-cycle-management tools.
• Working knowledge of functional safety, cybersecurity, component qualification, reliability, and supplier-management considerations for automotive electronics.
• Demonstrated ability to solve complex problems through independent analysis and cross-functional collaboration, influence technical decisions, and communicate effectively with customers and senior stakeholders.

By choice, we are committed to a diverse workforce - EOE/Protected Veteran/Disabled.

· FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology)

· AWIM (A World In Motion)

The Manager of Information Security leads Jama Software’s Information Security function and is responsible for ensuring the company’s security work is both strategically sound and operationally well-managed. This role requires a leader who can understand security best practices, interpret technical security information, assess risk, and make informed recommendations while also driving day-to-day execution across areas such as vulnerability management, incident response, security reviews, policy governance, and compliance readiness. The person in this role is expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy: identifying what needs attention, prioritizing the work, coordinating with the right stakeholders, communicating clearly, escalating blockers, and ensuring commitments are followed through to completion. They serve as a trusted security partner to Product, Engineering, IT, Legal, customer-facing teams, and senior leadership, translating complex security issues into practical business guidance and helping Jama maintain a mature, responsive, and reliable security posture.

What You'll Do:

• Lead the Information Security function, ensuring security programs are strategically aligned with business needs and operationally managed with clear owners, priorities, timelines, and follow-through.

• Own the day-to-day execution of core security programs, including vulnerability management, incident response, security risk assessment, policy governance, compliance readiness, and security reviews.

• Maintain clear visibility into active security issues, open findings, remediation plans, accountable owners, target dates, risks, decisions, and next steps.

• Lead timely security incident response, including initial triage, SIRT coordination, investigation, mitigation, stakeholder communication, documentation, and post-incident follow-up.

• Drive follow-up on penetration tests, security assessments, audits, customer findings, and other security reviews by identifying material risks, assigning owners, tracking remediation, and escalating blockers.

• Interpret technical security findings and translate them into clear risk assessments, recommendations, and action plans for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Develop, maintain, and operationalize security policies, standards, procedures, and guidance to support compliance obligations, customer expectations, and business priorities.

• Ensure security requests from internal stakeholders, customers, and auditors are acknowledged, triaged, routed, and closed in a timely and transparent manner.

• Serve as a trusted security advisor to Product, Engineering, IT, Legal, customer-facing teams, and senior leadership.

• Coordinate cross-functional initiatives that improve Jama’s security posture, reduce risk, and support compliance with SOC 2 Type II.

• Develop and maintain the Information Security roadmap, reflecting the emerging threats, customer expectations, regulatory requirements, audit findings, business priorities, and operational maturity needs.

• Support security awareness, training, and policy acknowledgement efforts in partnership with appropriate business owners.

• Evaluate and recommend security tooling, process improvements, and automation that improve visibility, response time, risk management, and operational effectiveness.

• Lead and develop members of the Information Security team through clear expectations, coaching, prioritization, feedback, and accountability.

What You'll Bring:

• 8+ years of experience in information security, including hands-on experience with security operations, risk management, incident response, vulnerability management, and compliance programs.

• 2+ years of people management experience, including setting expectations, coaching team members, prioritizing work, and holding others accountable for follow-through.

• Demonstrated experience owning or leading core security programs, such as vulnerability management, incident response, security risk assessment, policy governance, security reviews, and compliance readiness.

• Strong understanding of security best practices, application/product security concepts, cloud security, network fundamentals, and risk-based decision-making.

• Experience supporting SaaS products or hosted enterprise software environments, including partnership with Engineering, Product, IT, or infrastructure teams.

• Working knowledge of SOC 2 Type II and related security/compliance frameworks.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide timely stakeholder updates and concise executive-facing summaries.

• Demonstrated ability to operate autonomously, manage competing priorities, close communication loops, and follow work through to completion without requiring close day-to-day direction.

• Experience partnering cross-functionally with Legal, IT, Product, Engineering, customer-facing teams, auditors, and senior leadership on security matters.

Nice to Have:

• Experience with security automation, workflow improvement, or tooling that improves visibility, triage, remediation tracking, or reporting.

• Relevant security certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCSP, GIAC, or AWS Security Specialty

• Experience leading security work across distributed or remote-first teams

Perks and Benefits:

• Virtual first and culturally diverse work environment spanning 8 countries.

• Ambitious and fun work with a chance to define distinct, company-shaping tangible contributions.

• Flexible time off and leave programs crafted to meet the needs for your rejuvenation and extra support to cope with life events with a quarterly $75 wellness reimbursement.

jobs.title: Manager, Service Tooling and Equipment
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

As the Manager, Global Service Tooling & Equipment, you will lead the strategy, development, deployment, and ongoing management of the tools, equipment, and infrastructure that power Lucid's growing service network. Supporting more than 30 service locations across North America, you'll partner with Service Operations, Engineering, Facilities, Procurement, and Supplier partners to ensure technicians have the right tools, equipment, and resources to deliver exceptional customer experiences. From launching next-generation mobile service fleets and enabling new service centers to driving tooling readiness for future vehicle programs, this highly visible leadership role offers the opportunity to build scalable systems, lead critical programs, and directly influence Lucid's ability to service and support its rapidly expanding vehicle portfolio.

• Own the Global Service Tooling & Equipment program across 30+ North American service locations, supporting Service Centers, Mobile Service, Body Repair, field teams, and hundreds of technicians.

• Lead the development and deployment of a fleet of Mobile Service vehicle, including vehicle configuration, equipment layout, storage systems, compressors, power solutions, tooling packages, safety requirements, technician usability, prototyping, validation, and production rollout.

• Lead and develop the Service Tooling team, establishing clear ownership for daily tooling operations, ordering, deployment, inventory management, vendor coordination, tooling audits, and field support.

• Partner with Facilities and Service Operations on new Service Center readiness, including shop layouts, vehicle lifts, alignment and ADAS equipment, battery handling equipment, diagnostic systems, compressed air, specialty equipment, installation, commissioning, and launch.

• Own and continuously improve Lucid's Service Tooling Catalog and associated tooling-management systems, maintaining a centralized source of truth for approved tools, specifications, part numbers, suppliers, pricing, deployment status, and field requirements.

• Define Lucid's tooling strategy for existing and future vehicle platforms, including general service tooling, special service tools, diagnostic equipment, high-voltage equipment, shop equipment, lifting solutions, and restricted/safety-critical tooling.

• Partner with Engineering and Field Service Engineering to translate vehicle service requirements into scalable tooling solutions, ensuring tools are validated and available before vehicle and service-program launches.

• Own tooling readiness for new vehicle programs, identifying tooling requirements, validation plans, supplier lead times, deployment risks, technician requirements, and launch-readiness gates.

• Establish standardized tooling packages and equipment specifications for new and existing Service Centers to ensure consistency, technician productivity, safety, and cost control across the network.

• Manage strategic tooling and equipment suppliers from sourcing through deployment, including technical requirements, RFQs/RFPs, quotation review, commercial negotiations, purchase planning, delivery schedules, installations, issue resolution, warranty support, and supplier performance.

• Develop sourcing and standardization strategies that balance serviceability, technician usability, safety, cost, lead time, scalability, and total cost of ownership.

• Establish tooling request, approval, ordering, tracking, audit, and corrective-action workflows to maintain visibility and control as the service network scales.

• Develop and maintain processes for tooling audits, missing-tool recovery, restricted-tool control, loan tools, asset tracking, calibration, maintenance, and replacement planning.

• Monitor tooling and equipment readiness across the service network and proactively identify gaps that could impact vehicle repair capability, technician productivity, customer experience, or vehicle-program launches.

• Support field escalations and service campaigns requiring rapid development, sourcing, modification, or deployment of tools and equipment.

• Partner with Finance and Procurement to develop annual tooling budgets, forecasts, capital requirements, spend controls, and cost-reduction initiatives.

• Establish KPIs and reporting for areas such as tooling readiness, deployment status, supplier performance, order lead time, equipment uptime, audit compliance, launch readiness, spend, and program risk.

• Provide regular program updates to Service leadership, clearly communicating readiness, risks, dependencies, financial impact, and required decisions.

• Build scalable SOPs, operating playbooks, documentation, and governance that allow the Service Tooling organization to support Lucid's continued growth.

Qualifications

• 7+ years of experience in automotive service operations, service engineering, tooling and equipment, technical program management, fleet operations, manufacturing, or a related technical operations environment.

• 2+ years of experience leading people, programs, suppliers, or cross-functional technical teams.

• Strong understanding of automotive repair environments, technician workflows, service-center operations, tooling, shop equipment, and vehicle diagnostics.

• Demonstrated experience taking complex programs from requirements definition through sourcing, validation, deployment, and sustained operations.

• Strong program-management capability with experience managing multiple simultaneous projects, schedules, dependencies, budgets, risks, and stakeholders.

• Experience managing suppliers, sourcing technical equipment, evaluating quotations, negotiating commercial terms, and holding vendors accountable for quality, cost, and delivery.

• Ability to understand technical requirements and effectively communicate between technicians, engineers, suppliers, operations teams, and senior leadership.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to use data to evaluate readiness, utilization, cost, supplier performance, and operational risk.

• Experience developing standardized processes, SOPs, dashboards, tracking systems, and operational controls.

• Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment where requirements, vehicle programs, and priorities may change rapidly.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence across organizations without direct authority.

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting electric vehicles, high-voltage vehicle systems, advanced vehicle platforms, or EV service operations.

• Experience with new vehicle launches, prototype or pre-production vehicles, serviceability validation, or early fleet deployment.

• Experience developing or deploying mobile-service vehicles or other specialized fleet configurations.

• Familiarity with automotive lifts, alignment systems, ADAS calibration equipment, battery handling equipment, diagnostic equipment, compressed-air systems, and other automotive shop infrastructure.

• Experience supporting a geographically distributed service or field organization.

• Experience with tools such as Jira, Smartsheet, Coupa, Tableau, Excel, or similar program-management and business systems.

• Experience creating digital tooling catalogs, asset-management systems, procurement workflows, or operational dashboards.

ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. ZoomInfo is seeking a highly motivated Policy Analyst to join our Government & Regulatory Affairs team. You will work closely with internal leadership and external coalitions to evaluate legislative proposals, draft advocacy materials, and help shape our public policy positions in a rapidly evolving regulatory landscape.

• Advocacy & Drafting: Draft compelling outreach communications for advocacy and rulemaking, including memos, talk tracks, policy briefs, and presentation materials.

jobs.description:
As Scale continues to build and develop its field marketing and events program, we are looking for a Field Marketing & Events Manager to support our Frontier Data team in their event and field marketing initiatives. You’ll plan and run a wide range of events, from research conferences to Scale-hosted executive dinners and practitioner meetups, and support our annual flagship conference, the AI Leadership Summit.

You will join a rapidly growing team with the opportunity to manage and execute events from start to finish, drive lead generation, pipeline growth, and brand awareness, and plan event programming with the largest names in AI.

What you’ll do

• Execute end-to-end planning and logistics for executive dinners, meetups, happy hours, sponsored research conferences and trade shows, and virtual events.

• Design event programs that support sales goals, pipeline growth, and deal acceleration.

• Support event logistics for our annual flagship conference, the AI Leadership Summit.

• Manage event budgets and relationships with event production firms, contractors, and outside vendors.

• Partner with growth marketing on campaigns and MQL reporting.

• Work cross-functionally with sales and engineering to define event goals, shape content, and deliver against shared KPIs.

• Track event performance, measuring ROI and key metrics in Salesforce.

• Work with external executives and their teams to secure speakers and support their presentation planning.

What you’ll bring

• Experience fully managing and executing events ranging from small, intimate executive-level gatherings to large conferences with 1,000+ attendees.

• Experience planning and running executive dinners, VIP experiences, or similar high-touch events.

jobs.title: Profitability Manager - Labels and Packaging Platform
jobs.description:
The Profitability Manager drives business profitability through rigorous management of pricing execution, contract escalation, and margin recovery initiatives. Acting as a strategic partner to Finance, Operations, and Sales, this role transforms complex cost data into actionable commercial strategy. The manager will proactively optimize account portfolios by correcting negative-margin accounts and enforcing price pass-throughs, ensuring the business sustains long-term profitability post-implementation. The ideal candidate blends deep operational knowledge with commercial acumen, serving as a partner to sales teams to navigate pricing adjustments and protect margins.

Key Responsibilities:

Margin Optimization & Price Pass-Through Management

• Conduct rigorous portfolio reviews to systematically identify, triage, and improve profitability for margin-challenged accounts. This process effectively 'weeds the garden' by correcting underperforming portfolios, remediating accounts impacted by market inflation, and driving operational margin improvements.
• Monitor raw material cost trends, supply chain fluctuations, and operational inflation to execute systematic price pass-through updates and enforce contract escalation terms, CPI adjustments, and material cost-sharing clauses.
• Develop and maintain dynamic pricing models and acceptable margin thresholds to guide ongoing profitability for existing product lines and support account reviews.

Sales Alignment & Commercial Strategy

• This role focuses on post-win execution and ongoing commercial management rather than pre-sales activities, deal structuring, or initial pricing strategy.
• The position engages with accounts post-implementation to ensure long-term profitability through diligent margin maintenance and contract optimization.
• Responsibilities include translating complex cost structures into actionable post-production pricing adjustments, recovery plans, and articulating value propositions during contract renewals or price increase renegotiations.

Analytics, Dashboards & Reporting

• Maintain and expand existing analytical models and dashboards, while building new models as needed to track price realization, pass-through compliance, and margin expansion progress.
• Monitor contract expiration dates and track historical price adjustment implementation to proactively trigger renegotiation workflows.
• Utilize data to track account profitability trends and highlight high-risk accounts requiring immediate action.
• Provide weekly/monthly executive summaries detailing total margin recovered, outstanding price increases pending pass-through, and remaining negative-margin exposures.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Serve as the primary commercial point of contact for Operations and Finance to align pricing execution with real-time cost shifts and manufacturing efficiency goals.
• Facilitate regular reviews with Sales leadership to identify margin recovery opportunities and resolve account-level profitability gaps.
• Collaborate with Business Unit leadership on strategic margin improvement initiatives to drive continuous improvement in commercial performance.

• Education: HS diploma or equivalent required, Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Supply Chain, or a related field preferred.
• Experience: Minimum 3–5 years of progressive experience in pricing management, commercial operations, business analysis, or sales operations.
• Industry Knowledge: Proven understanding of internal company workflows, manufacturing/packaging cost drivers, and experience directly supporting or working within a sales environment.

Core Competencies & Skills

• Analytical Acumen: Capability to leverage, expand, and maintain existing analytical models, with the ability to aggregate data and build new actionable reporting dashboards in Excel or Google suite.
• Commercial & Negotiation Skills: Strong understanding of sales workflows, client contracting terms, price elasticity, and customer negotiation dynamics.
• Cross-Functional Leadership: Demonstrated ability to influence sales behavior, hold team members accountable, and drive change across operational and commercial groups.
• Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with the confidence to present recommendations directly to senior business leadership.
• Problem Solving: A proactive, creative problem solver capable of translating complex operational cost data into clear commercial action steps.
