jobs.title: Video & Content Lead
jobs.description:
Location: Boston area preferred. Northeast US with ability to travel to the Boston area is next preference if not in Boston. May consider alternative arrangements (hybrid)
Type: Independent Contractor (hourly or retainer)

**A note before you read further**

The world is changing fast, and so is this role. We can't fully tell you what this job looks like in six months. That's true of every role at Human Agency right now. What we need from you, no matter what: accountability, curiosity, and a builder-first mindset. If that sounds exciting, keep reading. If it sounds intimidating but you're still interested, let's talk. If none of that sounds like you, that's okay. This probably isn't your spot.

About Human Agency

We're scaling rapidly and have a growing pipeline of opportunities that demand exceptional talent across disciplines. Our mission is to bring on individuals, from creative producers to technical experts to entrepreneurial leaders, who can help us realize this next chapter of growth.

We are a company of doers. Leaders roll up their sleeves, teams work flat, and everyone contributes to what ships. Titles don't insulate us from feedback or basics. We invite critique, learn quickly, and keep raising the bar. The best ideas win here, no matter where they come from, because clients trust us to deliver the strongest outcomes every time.

Our clients' missions, products, and bottom lines are sacred. We immerse ourselves in their world, becoming stewards of their goals and partners in solving big problems. Every product, strategy, or asset we create must be both beautiful and functional; practical, usable, and designed for real-world impact.

Humans are our most valuable resource, and we only grow by hiring people who push us forward. Across strategy, engineering, design, data, and operations, we seek out teammates who raise the bar and make us better. Always hire up, never down.

We partner with organizations of all sizes to explore, design, and implement AI strategies that are secure, scalable, and human-centered. We believe AI should amplify human potential, not replace it, and we build with that conviction in every engagement. From advisory and tooling to implementation and education, we meet clients where they are and help them integrate AI in ways that align with their mission and values. Our goal is to empower teams to work smarter, move faster, and unlock new possibilities through thoughtful, responsible innovation.

And through it all, we lead with purpose, love, and adventure. We do meaningful work with people we care about, and we make the ride an adventure worth taking. Because at Human Agency, who we are and how we work are one and the same.

The Opportunity

Human Agency is building a content engine, and we need someone who can run it. Not a coordinator who farms out work, not a generalist who dabbles in video. A real craftsperson: someone classically trained in video editing who has kept that obsession alive outside of their day job, making things because they can't help it.

This role exists because we have stories worth telling (about AI, about the humans leading this transformation, about the organizations we work with), and we need someone who can capture, shape, and distribute those stories across every format that matters. Podcasts. Short-form. Long-form. Editorial thought leadership. We want someone who can go from working a camera to managing up to a founder to elevate their story. You're a humanistic storyteller who also understands media and content type.

The best version of this role isn't someone who waits for direction, it's someone who watches a rough interview, sees the four moments that matter, cuts them into something undeniable, and pitches three more angles we hadn't thought of. You'll work closely with leadership, which means fast feedback loops, high standards, and genuine creative collaboration. If that sounds like the best kind of pressure, keep reading.

What You'll Own

• Podcast Production: Edit and produce two-to-four podcast episodes per month, from raw audio and video to polished, publish-ready episodes (including sound design, sequencing, and any supporting assets).

• Short-Form Social Content: Cut long-form source material into compelling short-form pieces every month (the kind that stop a scroll, not just fill a feed).

• Documentary & Long-Form Projects: Take on occasional long-form production work, from shoot support through final cut.

• Editorial Judgment: Identify the moments inside raw recordings that carry weight, and build around those (structurally, rhythmically, and narratively).

• Content Distribution: Handle production for relevant platforms; understand how format, framing, and metadata affect reach and retention.

• Creative Contribution: Bring your own ideas to the table (better angles, stronger hooks, and production choices we wouldn't have thought to ask for).

Who You Are

Experience & Skills

• Classically trained video editor with a professional body of work that demonstrates technical depth, not just proficiency with the tools.

• Fluent in industry-standard editing software (Premiere Pro, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve, or equivalent), and fast enough to meet a real production schedule.

• Demonstrated experience cutting podcasts and long-form interview content into tight, publishable episodes.

• Track record of taking long-form source material and extracting short-form social content that actually performs.

• Comfortable working across formats (YouTube, podcast platforms, LinkedIn, Instagram, etc.) and understands that what works on one doesn't work on all.

• Experience with thought leadership and editorial-style production; you know how to make ideas feel consequential on screen, not just competent.

• A personal or side project that shows you make content because you love it (a YouTube channel, a podcast, a documentary, a body of work you built for yourself).

Mindset & Traits

• You can receive a dump of raw material (interviews, voice memos, rough footage) and know what to do with it without needing a brief for every decision.

• You hold yourself to a standard that exists independent of what the client asks for; good enough isn't a phrase in your vocabulary.

• You move fast without getting sloppy, and you flag problems early instead of delivering late.

• You have opinions about what makes content work, and you're willing to make the case for them, then let the best idea win.

• You're built for ambiguity: scope shifts, timelines compress, and priorities rearrange; you adapt without drama.

• You want your fingerprints on something that matters, not just a clean reel and a steady invoice.

Compensation & Logistics

• Remote engagement with a strong preference for Boston-based candidates given the production context.

• Independent contractor relationship, structured as hourly or monthly retainer depending on fit and workflow.

• Some travel required for occasional shoots; flexibility to accommodate production scheduling is expected.

Equal Opportunity Commitment

Human Agency is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diverse perspectives and are committed to building inclusive, high-performing teams where everyone can do their best work.

jobs.title: Director, Business Development
jobs.description:
ABOUT CARDLESS

Cardless is a Series C consumer fintech that uses AI to make it easy for the world's largest brands to build credit cards into their ecosystems. Think Shopify, but for credit cards. Brands use Cardless to configure, launch, and grow credit card programs that delight their customers and strengthen their core business.

Customers include Coinbase, Bilt Rewards, Alibaba, Qatar Airways, and LATAM Airlines. Cardless powers cards on all three major networks (Visa, Mastercard, and American Express) and uses agentic servicing to operate at a fraction of the headcount and cost that traditional card issuers require.

Cardless raised a $60 million Series C led by Spark Capital in September 2025, bringing total funding past $170 million. The team is past 70 people and scaling toward profitability by year-end 2026.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Cardless grows by landing new brand partners — and landing brand partners requires someone who can build relationships before there is a deal to discuss, navigate the processes that larger organizations use to make significant strategic decisions, and persuade companies that already have a card program that there is a better way to run one. This role is that person.

As Director of Business Development, you will own the top of the Cardless commercial funnel. You will identify the right prospects, build the relationships required to get in the room, and drive the process from first conversation through a signed term sheet. This role reports to the Chief Business Officer of Cardless.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor role with a clear mandate: Build an organized pipeline, bring brands closer to conversion, and negotiate durable and lucrative deals. You will be evaluated on the quality and velocity of the opportunities you generate and move forward.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

Build New Partner Relationships

 - Identify and prioritize the brands most likely to benefit from a Cardless card program — drawing on market data, competitive intelligence, and your own network to build a high-quality prospect list.

 - Develop relationships with senior decision-makers at target companies over the time horizon that enterprise deals require — not just the inbound conversations that happen to come in.

 - Represent Cardless credibly and compellingly to executives at major consumer brands, financial institutions, and loyalty programs — most of whom will already have opinions about the card space.

 - Work with Marketing and Product to ensure the materials, demos, and narratives you bring to market reflect what Cardless actually does and where it is going.

Work the Consulting and RFP Channel

 - Build and maintain relationships with the consulting firms and networks that run RFP and vendor selection processes for large card program decisions.

 - Ensure Cardless is known, understood, and credibly represented in the processes these firms run — which requires ongoing relationship maintenance, not just responding to RFPs as they arrive.

 - Develop a point of view on which consulting firms are most active in the card space, which relationships matter most, and where Cardless should invest relationship-building resources.

 - Respond to formal RFP processes with materials that are accurate, compelling, and differentiated — working with the product, finance, and partnerships teams to pull together the right inputs.

Target Companies with Existing Card Programs

 - Identify companies that currently have card programs through incumbent issuers — and build the case for why Cardless represents a materially better partner.

 - Develop deep familiarity with the competitive landscape: what the major incumbent issuers offer, where they fall short, and what a company that has lived through a card program launch actually cares about.

 - Build relationships at these companies in a way that is respectful of existing contracts and focused on what comes next — not adversarial to their current partners.

 - Work with the product and partnerships teams to ensure the Cardless pitch is grounded in real product capabilities and backed by the performance of existing programs.

Own the Business Development Process

 - Manage a pipeline of prospects from first contact through signed agreement, with the discipline and rigor that enterprise sales requires — accurate forecasting, clear next steps, and no deals falling through the cracks.

 - Work with the leadership team to prioritize which opportunities to pursue and at what pace, given the constraints of the partnerships team that will need to execute what BD signs.

 - Diligently maintain the systems — CRM, contact databases, outreach cadences — that make BD operations repeatable and scalable as the team grows.

 - Provide regular, honest reporting on pipeline health, deal velocity, and the competitive dynamics you observe in the market.
   
   


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Experience

 - 7-10 years in business development, partnerships, or a sales role with meaningful exposure to financial services — ideally including time at a bank, card issuer, or payment network.

 - A demonstrated track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals — not just sourcing conversations, but owning the process from prospecting through signature.

 - Existing network in the card and payments space — relationships with decision-makers at consumer brands, financial institutions, loyalty programs, or the consulting firms that advise them.

 - Experience navigating formal RFP processes for financial services technology or infrastructure is a strong plus.

Skills and Competencies

 - Network and Relationship Building: You have spent years building relationships in the right places, and you know how to open a door that is not obviously open. Your network is a genuine competitive advantage, not a LinkedIn following.

 - Financial Services Fluency: You understand how card programs work — the economics, the players, the contract structures, the regulatory context — well enough to have a credible commercial conversation with a bank executive or a CFO.

 - Sales Process and Discipline: You run a clean pipeline. You know where every deal is, what the next step is, and what it will take to close it. You do not lose deals because something fell through the cracks.

 - Communication and Presence: You are effective in a room with senior executives. You can explain what Cardless does in two minutes and make it sound like the most obvious thing in the world. You can also write.

 - Competitive Intelligence: You stay current on what incumbents are doing, what new entrants are building, and how the market is evolving — and you use that knowledge to sharpen how Cardless is positioned.

 - Judgment and Autonomy: You can prioritize your own time across a large number of potential opportunities and make good calls about where to invest without needing to be managed at the activity level.
   
   


THIS ROLE IS NOT A FIT IF

 - Your background is primarily inbound sales or account management — this role requires the ability to generate cold pipeline through network and outbound effort, not manage relationships that someone else originated.

 - You do not have meaningful experience in financial services — a general enterprise sales background without exposure to banking, cards, or payments will not be sufficient for the conversations this role requires.

 - You are looking for a management role with a team to build — this is an individual contributor position, and the expectation is that you carry your own number before you hire under you.

 - You require remote or hybrid work arrangements.




WHY THIS ROLE

Cardless has found product-market fit, has live programs with major brands, and is growing fast. What it does not yet have is a dedicated business development function — the top of the commercial funnel has been driven by the founders and the CBO. This role is the first dedicated BD hire, which means the person who joins now will set the template for how Cardless does business development.

The strongest salespeople in financial services are typically selling products with a 30-year track record and a brand that opens doors for them. Cardless is asking for something harder: to sell a better version of a product that most of its prospects already have. If that challenge sounds more interesting than intimidating, this is the right role.




COMPENSATION

This role has an annual starting salary range of $175,000–$220,000 + equity + benefits. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skills, experience, and specific work location.




BENEFITS

We're proud to offer our team excellent benefits:

💸 Meaningful Start-up equity

🏥 100% health, vision & dental primary coverage

➕ 75% health, vision & dental dependent coverage

🍱 Catered lunches

🚎 $250/month Commuter benefit

👶 Parental leave

✈️ Team building events & happy hours

🌴 Flexible PTO with a minimum of 15 days off per year

🖥️ Apple equipment

💸 401k plan

 


LOCATION

We're headquartered in San Francisco, CA, with a beautiful office in Jackson Square. This role is in-office 5 days a week.

The Finance & Strategy team accelerates the growth of our business by implementing new opportunities and solutions. We partner with teams across the company to improve the profitability, scalability, and defensibility of our business model. We are looking for an Associate to join our US Marketplace Finance & Strategy team and help manage the financial performance of our business. You will own the rhythm of P&L reporting, planning, and investment management. You’ll translate performance and strategic decisions into clear, leadership-ready narratives that help us make efficient, data-driven decisions. The role requires judgment, adaptability, and strong partnership with cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, constantly changing environment.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

• 2-3 years of strategic finance, corporate finance, or investment banking experience in a high-growth technology sector

• Experience working on projects that require cross-functional collaboration and ability to influence partners at all levels within an organization

• Advanced Excel & financial modeling skills. Able to build robust financial models used by teams throughout the company, and to size opportunities and build business cases for pursuing new initiatives

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Growth
jobs.description:
About Engine

Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

Your Mission

As part of the Engine team, you'll play a vital role in an environment where innovation meets collaboration. Here's what you'll take charge of:

• Own Product-Led Growth: Craft and execute experimentation-driven strategies across onboarding, activation, retention loops, and monetization. You'll move the metrics that matter most: activation rate, time to value, product-qualified leads, net dollar retention, and expansion revenue.

• Build AI-Powered Experiences: Collaborate with engineering, design, data, and go-to-market partners to apply LLMs, predictive logic, and smart automation that reduce friction, personalize the journey, and get customers to value faster.

• Grow Every Account: Drive cross-sell and attach across hotels, flights, cars, and groups, and adoption of Direct Bill, FlexPro, and Rewards at the moment of need. Keep accounts booking through quiet stretches and team changes.

• Connect Product and Sales: Spot high-intent moments in the product and get those accounts to the right sales or account team fast, so self-serve and human help work as one motion.

• Lead Experimentation at Scale: Form hypotheses, design and run A/B tests, and partner with data teams to turn results into action. Test early, learn fast, and scale what works across Engine's travel and spend management platform.

• Align and Influence: Translate complex ideas into clear, compelling plans, rally cross-functional stakeholders around shared goals, and make sure every growth feature delivers a seamless, high-impact experience for Engine customers.

What You'll Bring to Engine

We're looking for someone who's ready to make an impact and grow alongside us:

• Experience: 5+ years of hands-on product management experience, ideally for a self-serve or product-led B2B product. You’ve owned a conversion or revenue metric and moved metrics in at least two of acquisition, activation, expansion, and retention.

• Skills: You're a problem-solver with strong analytical and experimentation skills. You're comfortable designing tests, interpreting results, and turning data into decisions, and you thrive in fast-paced, innovative environments.

• Tech-Savvy: You understand how to apply AI to prototype, ship small fixes, and interrogate data. You're fluent in experimentation/analytics tools, e.g. Amplitude, LaunchDarkly, SQL.

• Mindset: You're deeply curious, outcome-focused, and ready to roll up your sleeves, collaborate, and deliver results that matter.

• Influence: You translate complex ideas into clear, compelling plans and drive alignment across engineering, design, data, sales, account management, and marketing.

Applications for this role will be accepted through 02/08/2027 or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Base Pay Range

$181,100—$213,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation
We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

• Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions.

• Benefits: Check out our full list at engine.com/culture

• Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more

jobs.title: Analyst, Finance and Capital Markets - Battery Storage
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Plus Power is an energy storage market leader, with a market-leading 10+ GW portfolio across more than 25 states that will transform North American electric grids into cleaner and more versatile critical infrastructure.

Standalone energy storage is rapidly transforming the North American energy markets, because it is cheaper than new natural gas plants, faster to build than fossil peakers or transmission, and able to perform diverse energy services. Plus Power partners with electricity system operators, utilities, and investors to originate, develop, finance, own and operate standalone energy storage projects that provide critical services to the wholesale electric market. Plus Power’s team applies an intentional mindset to energy storage development by using a data-driven approach to development and operations.

At Plus Power, we are focused on solving hard climate problems, profitably.  We are growing fast, and value candidates who, like us, share a focus on setting high expectations, owning and learning from mistakes in the spirit of radical transparency, and are committed to internal partnering as a key element of our ideas meritocracy. Our team praises Plus Power’s culture and excels through our game-changing mission and supportive ecosystem.

About the Role

Plus Power is looking to hire a Finance and Capital Markets Analyst to join the company’s finance team. This individual will support all aspects of project finance transactions for Plus Power’s battery storage projects including construction financing, term debt/back-leverage and tax equity. Key responsibilities include creating and managing complex financial models, supporting the due diligence process, project management of financing deliverables, and coordinating with external financing parties to support the closing and funding of transactions. In addition, you will assist the finance team in bidding and structuring offtake agreements and executing on project acquisitions and project sales. This individual will get broad exposure to all aspects of the energy storage development and financing process and will collaborate with all functional teams across the company. This role includes significant responsibilities and room for growth within the company.

Key Responsibilities

• Transaction Support: Support all aspects of debt and tax equity financing transactions, including preparation of marketing materials, due diligence, management of external consultants, and financial modeling.

• Project Modeling: Own all aspects of project financial models throughout the project lifecycle, including development, construction and operations. Modeling activities include project optimization, offtake bidding, and sourcing and vetting model inputs with experts in various groups across the company (Development, Interconnection, Markets, EPC, Origination, Asset Management).

• Data Analytics & Tools: Support the creation of dashboards, reports, and analytics to support senior management decision making and reporting to corporate investors

• Market Analysis: Analyze macroeconomic and ISO-level trends, including impacts of tax law changes, interest rate environments, and broader sector trends, and their effect on the viability of the company’s portfolio.

• Cross-Functional Support and Collaboration: Collaborate with other teams within Plus Power to perform economic analysis and support key business decisions, including PPA pricing, optimization of project design, major equipment selection and O&M contract negotiation.

Skills & Qualifications

• Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering or related field

• 1-2 years of project finance transaction experience at a developer, investment bank, project finance lender, tax equity investor, or infrastructure investor; OR finance/technical degree from a rigorous undergraduate program and completion of (or willingness to complete) a financial modeling course

• Proficiency in the Microsoft Office suite, especially Microsoft Excel, including experience with project financial modeling

• Tax equity modeling experience a plus

• Specific experience in energy storage, renewables, or gas a plus

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively and effectively in a cross-functional environment with team members who are geographically dispersed

• Highly organized with impeccable attention to detail

• Experience managing large projects with multiple stakeholders on tight timelines

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill and present complex information clearly and succinctly to internal and external stakeholders, including financing counterparties.

• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build positive working relationships and interact effectively with individuals across a range of roles, seniority levels, and working styles

• Ability and desire to learn and take on responsibility quickly

• Location flexible with a preference for candidates based in or near San Francisco, Chicago, Brooklyn, or Seattle (where other finance team members are based)

Compensation, Location, and Benefits

Highly competitive total compensation from one of North America’s leading energy storage developers, owners, and operators, along with market-leading health benefits, 401(k) match, generous paid parental leave, flexible time off, work from home stipend, and other programs designed to support employees and their families.

Flexible work arrangements include work-from-home or hybrid options from Plus Power’s offices in The Woodlands, San Francisco, Chicago, Seattle, Brooklyn, Denver, Palm Beach Gardens, and Birmingham. While we are a remote-first company, we also have a highly engaged and connected culture, with opportunities to come together for in-person connection, professional development, and continued learning and growth.

The expected salary range* for this position begins at $105,000. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range based on several factors including, but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, geographic labor market, and other factors consistent with applicable law. This position is also eligible to participate in our annual bonus program.

The deadline* for applying to this role is 11/12/2026.

Plus Power is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds can thrive. Plus Power is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

*This information is provided in accordance with applicable law.

GTM ENGINEER - MARKETING @ CLAY

We're looking for someone to focus on elevating our top-of-funnel workflows; building automations that generate demand, qualify it faster, and surface which accounts are actually in-market. You'll sit at the intersection of GTM Engineering and the Marketing org, partnering closely with our Demand Gen, Lifecycle, and SDR teams to turn prospect and account data into proactive, measurable action. Strong candidates will be builders with a strong understanding of the marketing org motion: how demand gen, lifecycle, campaign, and SDR teams operate and what data they need to be effective. You will operate with high agency but ground yourself in what your stakeholders need to be successful.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and own top-of-funnel workflow automations like lead and account scoring, intent and buying-signal detection, inbound enrichment and routing, speed-to-lead triggers, and proactive outbound plays off marketing signal

 - Partner closely with Demand Gen, Lifecycle Marketing, and SDR leadership to translate business needs into automation requirements and iterate based on feedback

 - Own the instrumentation behind MQL definitions and the marketing funnel; build the insight layer that answers what converts, where leads stall, which sources and campaigns produce real pipeline, and whether our qualification criteria still hold

 - Build the connective tissue between Marketing and SDRs; lead lifecycle and handoff logic, routing and assignment rules, follow-up SLAs, and the feedback loop that tells marketing which leads were actually worth working

 - Build tooling that surfaces the right account and prospect context for SDRs at the right moment; before first touch, during inbound follow-up, and ahead of campaign and event pushes

 - Push the limits of Clay and extend our platform into new use cases, feed our product team innovative ideas, dogfood new features and; act as a practitioner evangelist of Clay infrastructure and GTM Engineering

 - Partner deeply with GTM leaders and frontline teams to understand how our demand motion works today and where it breaks

 - Own projects end-to-end, from discovery and prototyping through rollout, adoption, and iteration; identify opportunities to automate, augment, or redesign workflows using AI, data, and better systems design

 - Design systems that improve speed, visibility, data quality, and execution across the funnel; connect systems through APIs, webhooks, integrations, and automation layers so information moves cleanly across the stack

 - Measure performance, adoption, and business impact of what you build, then improve it over time

 - Act as an internal thought partner on the future of AI-native GTM systems

 - 


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - At least 6-10 years working in a combination of Marketing Ops, RevOps, GTM Engineering or other similar applied technical discipline

 - At least 3 years in Marketing Ops/Demand Gen Ops or GTM Engineering or equivalent

 - Experience building, developing or connecting core systems like Salesforce and adjacent GTM systems including hands on experience with marketing automation and inbound tooling such as HubSpot, Marketo, Customer.io http://Customer.io, or Braze, and intent/enrichment layers such as 6sense, Demandbase, Clearbit, or Common Room

 - Fluency with the mechanics of the marketing funnel; lead lifecycle design, scoring models, routing logic, attribution, deliverability and database health, and funnel conversion and velocity metrics

 - Proven ability to build and problem solve with methods incorporating Python, JavaScript, SQL, or TypeScript; we pull our own data on this team

 - Track record of deploying and building AI-powered internal tools, automations, or agentic workflows

 - Experience using data warehouses, BI tools, or event-driven systems

 - Executive presence -- you communicate concisely and confidently even about technical topics with non technical people while simultaneously communicating business requirements to technical audiences

 - Proven ability to operate effectively in ambiguous and fluid hypergrowth environments -- you not only embrace change but drive it

 - Experience building in Clay as a primary workflow or enrichment layer is not required but is highly preferred (successful candidates with no experience in Clay will show increasing proficiency throughout the interview process)

 - Bonus points for experience in analytics engineering, data science and /or programming languages

HEAD OF FIELD MARKETING @ CLAY

Roughly half of Clay's business now runs through a sales-led motion serving mid-market, enterprise, and strategic accounts, and we're building the marketing engine to match. You'll sit in the Growth team, work in a pod with sales leadership, Corporate Events, and RevOps, and be the single front door for anything the sales org needs from marketing events.  - Sit in sales leadership's staff meeting and pipeline reviews as marketing's field representative, and act as the single point of contact for all event requests from sales.

 - Co-own the decision to attend tier-one shows with Brand, and own the meeting and pipeline plan for each.

 - Stand up the measurement layer with RevOps so every program reports sourced pipeline, meetings booked, and target-account attendance, and compares on cost per opportunity against other growth channels.

 - Hire and manage field marketers as the sales org grows, starting with segment alignment and regionalizing as we build international sales coverage.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 10+ years in B2B marketing leading field or regional marketing at a company with a meaningful enterprise or strategic sales motion.

 - A track record of sourcing pipeline through account-targeted programs, and the numbers to show it.

 - Deep credibility with sales leaders; you've sat in their staff meetings and they've asked for you by name.

 - Experience running the pipeline layer inside a user conference or tier-one show alongside a brand or events team.

 - Operational rigor: you build target lists, funding rules, and reporting before you book venues.

 - You are AI forward: you use agents and automation to run programs leaner than the headcount suggests.

 - Strongly preferred: experience building in Clay.

jobs.title: Clinical Quality Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Eikon Therapeutics is a new biopharmaceutical company employing revolutionary technology at the intersection of chemistry, engineering, computation, and biology to discover novel treatments for life-threatening diseases. Eikon’s discovery platform is built on groundbreaking innovations from its founders (Nobel Prize, 2014), culminating in the creation of microscopes which enable real time, molecular-resolution measurements of protein movement in living cells, thereby unlocking otherwise intractable classes of proteins as drug targets.

Position

In partnership with the Director of Process Management for Clinical Research & Development, to whom this role reports, the Clinical Quality Operations Manager (CQOM) is accountable for the execution of operational quality management and inspection readiness activities across assigned clinical programs within Eikon’s clinical development portfolio. The CQOM oversees clinical quality operations across assigned clinical programs, embedding quality-by-design (QbD) principles, risk-based quality plans, and vendor oversight into Eikon’s clinical trials. This includes ensuring consistent execution of QbD principles across assigned clinical studies, facilitating identification of Critical to Quality (CtQ) factors and associated risk assessments, and establishing and actively maintaining study-specific quality plans throughout the study lifecycle using a risk-based approach. The CQOM is accountable for maintaining inspection readiness through disciplined execution of risk assessments, quality plans, and operational standards, in collaboration with Clinical Quality Assurance (CQA) on inspection preparation, management and follow-up activities.The successful candidate will work closely with cross-functional Clinical Research & Development teams to ensure successful completion of studies within timelines and budget, with a focus on exquisite quality to support operational excellence and world-class in-house clinical study management.

This role requires onsite presence at minimum 3 days per week in our Millbrae, CA or Jersey City, NJ offices to support effective management, operational excellence, and high-performance delivery of clinical studies and expected team growth & collaboration.

About You

You are a collaborative, hands-on quality operations professional who enjoys working alongside clinical study teams to strengthen consistency, embed quality and drive disciplined trial execution. You bring credibility through deep knowledge of GCP and strong clinical operations expertise and are energized by cross-functional partnership. You are excited about the opportunity to help shape a new function in a growing organization.

What You’ll Do

• Ensures consistent execution of ‘quality by design’ principles in assigned clinical trials. Reviews Risk Assessment and Categorization Tools (RACTs), quality plans, and study-specific procedures with Study Management Teams to confirm accuracy, compliance with Sponsor requirements, and inspection-readiness.

• Facilitates review of CtQs, quality plans and risk mitigation approaches to identify inconsistencies, emerging signals, and trends and to provide relevant feedback to the Head of Clinical Study Management and Director of Process Management for Clinical R&D, as appropriate.

• Works with Clinical R&D peers to analyze data across Eikon’s clinical trials to identify signals and trends and translate findings into actionable process improvement strategies.

• In partnership with the Director of Process Management for Clinical R&D, the Head of Clinical Data Analytics and Reporting and the Head of Clinical Study Management, builds proficiency in leveraging technology and data to recognize and respond to new and emerging risks across assigned clinical programs, including how GCP applies to digital data management and novel trial technology.

• Partners with cross-functional study teams to ensure vendor and CRO performance is documented in vendor and CRO oversight plans and monitored against quality expectations, escalating compliance, or inspection-readiness risks to Clinical R&D functional area Heads, as necessary.

• Builds and enables effective working relationships with key stakeholders to ensure and maintain role clarity and business effectiveness. This will include ongoing partnership with Clinical Quality Assurance (CQA) and acting as the link between Clinical R&D functional areas, clinical study teams, enterprise business functions, and regional study management.

• Contributes to the standardization of Clinical Quality Operations procedures, tools, and templates to ensure consistency and seamless progression throughout the study lifecycle.

Inspection Preparation and Management

• Maintains current, working knowledge of global GCP inspection practices – including requirements from FDA, EMA, MHRA, and other established and emerging authorities – to effectively support GCP inspections worldwide. May serve as point of contact for a specific regulatory area (e.g., FDA, EMA, NMPA). Is responsible for monitoring, interpreting, and communicating relevant regulatory developments.

• Maintains current awareness of filing schedules, potential future inspections, and ongoing inspection preparation activities.

• Supports CQA in developing, updating, and maintaining GCP inspection procedures and guidelines within Clinical Development Operations and Clinical R&D functional areas.

• Contributes to the development and/or revision of Eikon policies, SOPs, and training materials.

• Ensures the operational foundation supports favorable inspection outcomes and that study teams execute consistently against study plans and operational standards.

• Partners with CQA to ensure the Clinical R&D functional areas are fully informed and prepared to support Regulatory Health Authority inspections led by CQA, worldwide.

• Escalates potentially significant compliance risks/impact to Clinical R&D functional area Heads, as necessary.

CAPA Management Support

• Leads CAPA implementation for CQA-sponsored internal audits for assigned studies, partnering with study teams and functions to translate findings into process changes.

• For external audits and Regulatory Health Authority inspections, partners with study teams to develop CAPA responses and implement CQA-approved corrective actions requiring process, tool, or workflow changes.

• Coordinates education and training for study teams on process changes resulting from CAPAs, ensuring changes are understood, adopted, and sustained in practice.

Other Activities

• Provides RACT completion status, quality plan metrics, and other operational data to CQA for inclusion in GCP Quality Council meetings.

• Assesses and provides input to strengthen company programs/strategies with an aim to increase inspection readiness.

• Facilitates and/or supports remediation, prevention, and process improvement activities, including training, as needed.

Qualifications

• Minimum of 6+ years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 4+ years of experience with a post graduate degree. Additional certifications such as lean six sigma or PMP are preferred but not required.

• Strong working knowledge of GCP, ICH E6(R3) guidelines and other relevant regulations and guidelines.

• Experience with CAPA management, including root cause analysis, preventive action development, translating CAPA findings into operational changes and tracking commitments to completion.

• Experience with risk management tools and quality planning in clinical development, including Quality by Design and risk-based approaches.

• Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with clinical operations, quality assurance, regulatory, data management, and other clinical development teams in a matrixed environment.

• Strong oral and written communication skills in an international environment with the ability to influence at all levels.

• Strong teamwork and leadership skills, including conflict resolution expertise.

• Ability to analyze, interpret and solve complex problems.

• Ability to think strategically and objectively while applying creativity and innovation.

• Ability to synthesize findings and deliver lessons learned.

• Experience with Veeva or similar document and quality management systems is a plus.

At Eikon, employee compensation also includes bonus and equity compensation, in addition to several generous benefit programs, including:​

• 401k plan with company matching​

• Medical (premiums covered by Eikon at 95%), dental and vision insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%)​

• Mental health and wellness benefits​

• Weeklong summer and winter holiday shutdowns​

• Generous paid time off and holiday policies​

• Life/AD&D Insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%) and optional supplemental employee-paid life/AD&D policies ​

• Enhanced parental leave benefit​

• Daily subsidized lunch program when on-site​

The expected salary range for this role is $143,000 to $173,250 depending on skills, competency, and the market demand for your expertise.

Eikon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment.

We are currently not accepting any new third-party agencies or firms at this time. Please do not forward unsolicited agency resumes to our website, employees or Human Resources. Eikon Therapeutics will not pay fees to any third-party agency or firm associated with unsolicited resumes.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Client Account Manager

Location: New York, NY, Atlanta, GA, or Remote, USA

Exemption Status: Full-time, exempt

Who We Are

Impiricus is the Agentic Commercialization Platform for Healthcare. We help life sciences teams understand physician intent, coordinate the right clinical and commercial resources, and enable real-time action when HCPs need support. Our AI-powered platform acts as a field force multiplier: extending reach between rep visits, prioritizing the highest-impact path for each physician, and connecting HCPs to coverage, evidence, medical information, patient support, MSLs, field teams, samples, and approved content in the moments that matter.

Founded by a practicing physician and a senior pharmaceutical executive, Impiricus was built to accelerate patient access to life-saving treatments through ethical, physician-first engagement. More than one million opted-in HCPs trust Impiricus as a preferred channel, including many who are underserved or hard to reach through traditional outreach. Products such as the Intelligently Optimized Network (ION), Pulse, Spark, and Ascend work together so every interaction can move from information to action. Guided by our Physician Advisory Board, we keep engagement clinically meaningful, compliant, and grounded in better patient care.

Job Summary:

Impiricus is seeking a dynamic Client Account Manager to be the first dedicated client services hire for DocUpdate, supporting Curated, our physician engagement and matchmaking platform. Curated connects physicians with meaningful non-clinical opportunities, including advisory boards, consulting engagements, market research, expert calls, and other professional collaborations across healthcare.

You will be the primary relationship owner for your accounts and manage the client experience from initial intake through successful delivery, serving as the bridge between our clients and the Curated operations team. Your clients will span legal, AI labs and technology companies, medtech, CROs, biotech, locum tenens and staffing, health systems and IDNs, and other industries outside of pharma. You will also be the day-to-day partner for Impiricus’s client services teams, who bring pharma programs onto Curated; those programs run through Curated independently of Impiricus’s commercial teams.

This is a true ground-floor role. There is no existing playbook for client services within DocUpdate, and you will help write it. We are looking for someone who is proactive, resourceful, and commercially curious, who builds trusted relationships easily and is energized by creating structure where it doesn’t yet exist. As Curated scales, so will the team around you, and the people who shape the foundation are the ones we look to as the business grows.

Responsibilities

Client Relationship Management

• Serve as the primary point of contact for a portfolio of Curated clients across legal, AI and technology, medtech, CRO, locum tenens, health system, and other non-pharma industries, building trusted, long-term relationships.

• Partner day to day with Impiricus’s client services teams as they bring pharma programs onto Curated, helping them scope, launch, and deliver with a consistent, high-quality experience.

• Guide clients through the full lifecycle of a physician engagement program, from intake and scoping through physician sourcing, scheduling, delivery, and follow-up.

• Understand each client’s objectives and ensure projects are delivered with exceptional service and attention to detail.

• Proactively communicate project updates, timelines, risks, and next steps while maintaining a high-touch client experience.

• Identify opportunities to deepen relationships and expand partnerships over time, from repeat engagements to new use cases.

Program & Project Coordination

• Partner closely with internal Curated operations teams to coordinate physician recruitment, scheduling, compensation, and project execution.

• Manage multiple concurrent client engagements across different industries while ensuring timelines and deliverables remain on track.

• Coordinate cross-functional communication between Operations, Product, Finance, Legal and Compliance, and other internal stakeholders, honoring the separation between Curated’s client work and Impiricus’s commercial teams.

• Monitor project health and proactively resolve issues before they impact clients.

• Maintain accurate documentation and project information within CRM and project management systems.

Building the Function

• Act as the founding member of Curated client services: define how intake, onboarding, communication standards, escalation, and reporting work for external clients and internal partners alike.

• Turn what you learn from every engagement into repeatable playbooks, templates, and tooling that let the business scale without losing the high-touch experience.

• Be the voice of the client inside the company, bringing insights to Product and Operations that shape the platform and what we offer.

• Support onboarding of new clients and contribute to a consistently exceptional customer experience.

• Demonstrate leadership potential, with the opportunity to grow into a people leadership role, hiring, developing, and guiding the team as the business scales.

Education & Experience

Required

• Bachelor's degree required, or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.

• 5+ years of experience in Account Management, Client Success, Customer Success, Strategic Accounts, or a related client-facing role.

• Experience within healthcare technology, medtech, digital health, SaaS, marketplaces, or another complex B2B environment.

• Proven ability to manage multiple client relationships simultaneously across different industries while delivering exceptional customer experiences.

• Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to prioritize competing demands.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong executive presence.

• A record of ownership: you have built or improved a process, program, or team function without being asked, and you are comfortable in a fast-paced, evolving environment with limited structure.

• Experience using CRM platforms such as HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar customer management systems.

Preferred

• Experience supporting clients across healthcare, medtech, biotech, AI, legal, staffing, or life sciences organizations. Familiarity with expert networks, market research, advisory boards, or other physician engagement models. Experience working with Integrated Delivery Networks (IDNs) or health systems. Experience collaborating across Sales, Operations, Product, and Finance, or serving internal teams as customers. Previous experience helping build or scale client-facing processes, or a client services team, within a growing organization.

Compensation and Benefits

The base salary for this role is $95,000 - $115,000.

Where you land within the range will reflect your skills, experience, and location, while keeping team parity in mind and leaving room for future growth.

Important Notice

To protect candidates, please note that all communication from our team will come directly from an @impiricus.com email address. We do not engage third party recruiters to schedule interviews for this role. If you receive outreach from anyone outside of our domain claiming to represent Impiricus, please disregard and let us know by forwarding the message to careers@impiricus.com

Benefits:

Impiricus focuses on taking care of our teammates’ professional and personal growth and well-being.

Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents + on-demand healthcare concierge
HSA, FSA & DCFSA: Pre-tax savings options for healthcare and dependent care, with monthly employer contributions to HSA (if enrolled in a high-deductible plan)
Coverage & Protection: 100% paid short- and long-term disability, plus life and AD&D insurance
Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need with a flexible vacation policy — recharge your batteries your way
Parental Leave: Paid parental leave to spend time with your newborn, adopted, or foster child (available after 6 months)
Your Work, Your Way: If you’re close to an office, we encourage spending some time in-person to collaborate and connect. If not, remote is always an option.
401(k): Save for your future with tax advantages (and company match!)

jobs.title: STEAM Project Designer, K-12 Education
jobs.description:
The Curriculum Developer designs the imagination-sparking STEAM projects and curriculum at the heart of every Galileo educational product. The job includes carrying an idea from initial prototype — say, a cardboard castle with a working drawbridge — through testing and refinement, to a gif-based facilitation guide an instructor can pick up and teach with confidence. While the role is primarily focused on curriculum development and production, it also includes developing and delivering instructor training.

For 25 years, Galileo has been offering best-in-class, STEAM-based summer camps that build creative confidence, growth mindset, and innovation skills for kids from kindergarten through eighth grade. Today, we serve kids at nearly 100 flagship Camp Galileo sites and now, through Galileo X Solutions, also empower school district staff and community-based organizations to deliver our programs for their summer, afterschool, or intersession offerings.

This role sits within the Educational Product team — the group that builds the programs, tools, and systems that make Galileo educational enrichment experiences possible — and reports to the Director of Educational Product. The Curriculum Developer works closely with other Educational Product team members and partners with the Supply Chain team to curate and specify instructional materials.

Success in this role requires serious creativity and tinkering skills, an approach to development grounded in the real needs of instructors and the children they teach, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced production environment. It also calls for big-picture thinking while still sweating the smallest details, and the openness to embrace an iterative and feedback-driven, collaborative design process.

Why this Role Matters

Every Galileo lesson reaches thousands of educators and tens of thousands of children.

That impact starts with a kernel of an idea — a mini golf game with paint-stirrer walls, a secret safe with a pneumatic deadbolt, a rideable rocking pet made from a reinforced cardboard box — that the Curriculum Developer might dream up on a Tuesday afternoon. From there, it becomes a catalyst that shapes what materials get ordered, what instructors say in the classroom, and what kids actually build with their own two hands.

There are intangible impacts too.

For kids: building Galileo projects enables them to pursue their own ideas, solve their own problems, and develop lasting confidence in their ability to create.

For new instructors: using our carefully crafted facilitation guides might help them discover they love teaching, and inspire them to launch a career in education.

For Galileo: the quality of our curriculum is a key driver of our success as a business. Our signature projects attract families to our camps. Instructors return year after year because the curriculum sets them up to succeed. School districts partner with us and renew because our program is unique and delivers on its promise.

The Curriculum Developer sets all of this in motion.

You will be Accountable For

Designing the Projects

• Dream up, tinker, and perfect hands-on STEAM projects that inspire kids, delight their families, and differentiate Galileo programs from the rest.
• Test activities in classroom settings to refine lesson pacing and project steps, and ensure building techniques are age-appropriate.
• Specify the materials needed for each project — down to the exact number of craft sticks and inches of tape. Collaborate with the Supply Chain team to approve samples and meet all program constraints.

Building the Facilitation Guides and Training

• Create clear, multimedia facilitation guides that are grounded in the Galileo Innovation Approach and support instructors to implement the program with ease.
• Design — and sometimes deliver — instructor training that builds excitement for Galileo’s programs and prepares facilitators to deliver them with fidelity.

Driving Continuous Improvement

• Get out in the field to observe the programs in action. Talk with instructors about what is and isn't working, and obsess over survey data and customer feedback. Turn those findings into insights that inform future development.

Contributing to Educational Product

• Support a range of Educational Product team priorities as needed —E.g. new curriculum templates to support instructional best practices, applications for accessing and distributing content, professional development for Camp Directors/ Site Leaders, tools and resources for program operations, etc,
• Take initiative to expand into new areas of Educational Product design as personal goals align with the team's needs.

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience to demonstrate subject matter expertise in education, art and design, engineering, or related fields.
• 3+ years in educational settings, specifically designing hands-on activities that engage students in creative problem-solving.
• Experience creating multimedia content, including basic photography and video production.
• Understanding of K-8 enrichment environments, educator needs, and kids' developmental capacities.
• A deep well of STEAM project ideas and a proven track record of bringing those ideas to life.
• Experience meeting regular deadlines in a dynamic, fast-paced production environment.
• A track record of developing clear instructional materials and effectively communicating complex ideas.

We strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences, and we are committed to equitable and inclusive hiring practices. If you think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply!

Work Location

Bay required: This position would be based in the Bay Area. Galileo Headquarters, 111 Myrtle St., Oakland, CA 94607. Galileo currently adheres to a hybrid office and work from home policy. More information to be provided during the interview stage.

HQ staff may be expected to visit camp locations or clients to experience Camp Galileo and Galileo X Solutions first-hand. Occasionally, onsite events or meetings may also be required. 10% travel may be required, depending on location.

Schedule & Time Commitment

This is a full-time position, averaging 40 hours per week. While we prioritize work-life balance, there may be times when additional hours are necessary to meet deadlines and ensure the success of our programs.

Compensation

We anticipate total compensation for this Full-Time, exempt position to be $70,000 - $80,000 plus eligibility to earn a 5% bonus annually beginning the first January after a full season in this role.

Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and professional experience.

Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Benefits

We offer comprehensive benefits that reflect our commitment to supporting diverse needs:

• No-cost medical insurance for employees (additional plans and options to add dependents available at cost)
• Vision and Dental Insurance
• 401k benefits after 1 year of employment
• Flexible Paid Time Off - time off is not limited, and we strongly recommend that employees take time off to rest and recharge.
• Unlimited free camp for your child(ren), OR two free weeks to be gifted (including AM/PM Extended Care)
• Friends and Family Discount for Galileo Camps
• Priority scholarship nominations for Galileo Camps
• Generous parental leave and extensive support with leave planning
• Employee Assistance Program, options for life insurance, and more!

Please note that our job descriptions are a summary of the typical functions of the job, not an exhaustive or comprehensive list of all possible responsibilities, tasks, and duties.

We comply with the ADA and provide reasonable accommodations that allow qualified applicants/employees to perform the essential functions of the job. To request an accommodation, contact our Human Resources team.

During the onboarding process, in accordance with applicable local and state requirements, you may be required to complete a Tuberculosis (TB) screening, background check(s), and state-mandated training(s). More details will be provided during your onboarding process.

Physical Demands

• operate a computer (including typing, reading)
• Seeing, hearing, and speaking, both nearby and at a distance
• Use hands and fingers to help with classroom supplies and operate equipment
• Frequent standing, walking, kneeling, and sitting

**RECRUITERS DO NOT CONTACT**

At Chicago Collision Attorneys, we pride ourselves on being Chicago's trusted personal injury firm, dedicated to advocating for our clients' rights with integrity and persistence. Our seasoned team has recovered millions for clients facing a range of personal injuries. Our focus on car accidents, wrongful deaths, and catastrophic injuries ensures that clients receive the expertise and personal care they deserve.

Our firm operates from its River North, Chicago location, with a diverse and collaborative team. We have integrated domestic and international talent, reflecting our commitment to inclusivity and innovation. Our attorneys are at the Daley Center daily, fighting tirelessly to ensure that each client's voice is heard and that justice is served. We intentionally limit caseloads across our entire team to ensure personalized attention and exceptional advocacy for every client.

The Director of Intake at Chicago Collision Attorneys will be pivotal in reshaping the way our firm manages client interactions from the first point of contact. This role is not just about overseeing day-to-day operations but about strategically leading the intake team to streamline processes, enhance client experience, and support our firm's mission of delivering outstanding legal service. The Director will play a crucial role in increasing lead conversion, standardizing procedures, and implementing innovative solutions to drive client advocacy and satisfaction.

What you’ll do:

• Team Leadership: Guide and develop a three-member global intake team, fostering strong connections and efficient workflow.

• Process Standardization: Implement standardized scripts and processes for consistent client communication and improved client experiences.

• KPI Development & Reporting: Establish, implement, and track meaningful intake KPIs, build dashboards and recurring reports, and translate performance data into actionable insights for leadership.

• Hands-On Intake: Personally handle intake calls daily, support mid-level problem calls, stay close to the client experience, and identify opportunities to improve scripts, follow-up, and conversion.

• Client Experience Enhancement: Design and refine the intake and onboarding experience so new clients feel reassured, supported, and confident they made the right decision from the first call forward.

• Lead Conversion Improvement: Improve prioritization, follow-up, and conversion of organic and referral-based leads by standardizing questions, workflows, and follow-up expectations.

• Call Quality Assurance: Oversee call quality through regular reviews and a structured scorecard system to maintain high standards.

• Automation Collaboration: Work with in-house developers to maximize efficiency with automated processes and lead scoring systems.

• Operational Projects: Take ownership of select cross-functional operational initiatives, including vendor research, administrative process improvement, and other strategic projects as the role expands.

• Incentive Program Design: Create a motivational structure that rewards performance, aligns with KPIs, and addresses team preferences.

What we’re looking for:

• Leadership Experience: Approximately 3 to 5 years of experience in intake or another high-volume client service environment, with demonstrated people management, coaching, or team leadership experience.

• Industry Background: Legal experience is not required. Candidates from other high-volume intake, client service, medical, or similar environments are encouraged to apply.

• Strategic Skills: Demonstrated ability to develop and implement KPIs, improve process efficiency, and coach team members.

• Tech-Savvy: Comfortable using CRM and phone systems such as Filevine and RingCentral, reviewing intake calls, interpreting data, and partnering with internal engineering resources to improve automation and reporting.

• Empathy and Communication: High emotional intelligence with strong communication skills to manage client interactions and team dynamics.

• Problem-Solving Ability: Strong critical thinking skills to identify and address process inefficiencies independently.

• Global Team Leadership: Comfortable leading and developing an international team; prior experience managing offshore or global employees is a plus.

• Location Requirement: This is a full-time, onsite role based in River North, Chicago.

Why you should work here:

• High Impact Role: Lead a key function that drives the firm's client engagement and operational success.

• Growth Opportunities: Potential to advance into broader operational leadership roles as you demonstrate impact and build trust.

• Autonomy and Innovation: Freedom to introduce new approaches, partner with leadership, and directly influence firm strategy.

• Collaborative Culture: Join a team that values compassion, empathy, and innovation, creating meaningful contributions to client advocacy.

Additional perks:

• Compensation: Target salary range of $80,000 to $100,000, with flexibility above this range for exceptional candidates whose experience and capabilities support broader operational ownership.

• Generous PTO: Four weeks of paid time off annually plus six holidays during the first year.

• Retirement Savings: Participate in a 401(k) plan with a 3% employer match for future security.

• Health Support: A healthcare stipend or similar reimbursement arrangement will be discussed during the interview process.

• Flexible Scheduling: Standard hours are approximately 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, with reasonable flexibility around start and end times based on business needs.

Join Chicago Collision Attorneys as the Director of Intake, where you'll play an essential role in transforming client interactions and supporting our firm's mission of justice and advocacy. If you're ready to innovate, lead, and make a real difference, we invite you to apply and become a part of our dynamic team.

jobs.title: Analyst Relations
jobs.description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring an analyst relations manager for ElevenAgents in North America. We're looking for someone who has built an AR function from the ground up and knows what that program looks like once it's actually working – not just briefings on a calendar, but a real point of view that analysts trust and come back to.

Part of that point of view is getting analysts ahead of where ElevenAgents is taking the market – an enterprise-grade platform for deploying voice and chat agents at scale.

We already have a relationship with Gartner – the next phase is turning that into our first Magic Quadrant inclusion, and building that same muscle with Forrester and IDC as we expand coverage in 2027. You'll work directly with our Growth, Research and Field Deployment Engineering teams to understand what we're actually building, and turn that into a narrative analysts can act on.




REQUIREMENTS

 - Experience running or building an analyst relations function, ideally in enterprise software, AI, or CX/contact center technology.

 - Direct, hands-on experience taking a company through a Gartner Magic Quadrant or Forrester Wave. You know what the submission process actually demands and you're ready to bring that same rigor to ElevenLabs.

 - Able to shape category narrative for a company that spans multiple product lines - helping analysts see how ElevenAgent – and eventually ElevenCreative, and ElevenAPI – add up to one coherent market position.

 - Comfortable prepping executives and technical leads for analyst inquiries and briefings, and building the cadence – newsletters, check-ins, event presence like Gartner IT Symposium – that keeps analysts current between them.

 - Bonus: experience covering agentic AI, voice AI, or conversational AI categories specifically.


GROWTH POTENTIAL

We believe in hiring the best talent in the world to make an impact in the right role at the right time. At ElevenLabs, strong performance creates opportunities for growth. Here are some of the career paths you can expect after excelling in this role:

 - Expand ownership from North America to a global analyst relations remit as we grow Forrester and IDC coverage in 2027.

 - Grow into a broader analyst and industry relations leadership role spanning ElevenAgents, ElevenCreative, and ElevenAPI as the function scales.


LOCATION

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in North America with the ability to operate in PT or ET timezones. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in New York or San Francisco.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

You will own the full sales cycle—from prospecting through deal closure—and build strategic relationships with senior financial services decision-makers.
