We don't just deliver insights; we empower businesses to make decisions that move revenue.

With $370M in Series C funding and over $100M in ARR, we are scaling at lightspeed. Our 850+ teammates across 35 countries aren't just building software—they are leveraging cutting-edge AI to help hoteliers be the first to act. Tens of thousands of hotels across 185 countries trust Lighthouse to execute their commercial strategy, including every one of the top 15 global chains and thousands of independent hotels that consistently outperform their markets. With Lighthouse AI, the intelligence gets deeper. Decisions get smarter. Actions get faster. We help hoteliers be first to act.

Lighthouse Values: Our guiding light

We are Lumineers. Our shared values keep us on a collaborative path fostering a cultural and customer centric environment

• Pursuit of greatness: We’re innovators who care deeply about our customers’ success. Our team brings their best work, stays curious, and delivers excellence through attention to detail

• Meaningful work matters: We make every moment count by knowing what to deliver, why it matters, and how it drives Lighthouse forward

• Elevate each other: We don’t just work together - we grow together. What unites us is understanding each other as people and working toward shared goals

We’re more than just a workplace – we’re a community. Collaborative, fun, and deeply committed, we work hard together to revolutionize the hospitality sector. Are you ready to join us and shine brighter in the industry’s most exciting rocket-ship? 🚀

Job Details

• 💼 Revenue

• 📍 United States - Dallas, TX

• 🕜 Full-Time/Hybrid

• 💰 $65,000.00 - $79,500.00 (Commission: $113,000.00 - $127,500.00 OTE)

What you will do

You’ll be the face of Lighthouse for independent hotels, owning the full sales cycle from prospecting to close. This is a hunter role: you carry a quota, you build your own pipeline, and you’re accountable to outcomes and success. No excuses, just results.

For independent properties with limited staff and time, every pricing decision, missed opportunity, or manual task adds up quickly. When AI takes repetitive work off their plate and helps hoteliers act faster, the impact is felt almost immediately.

You will be selling a comprehensive suite of AI-driven tools designed specifically to streamline and elevate independent hotel operations. You'll empower hoteliers to replace manual guesswork with automated pricing and reservation management, ultimately helping them drive up to 21% more revenue. This means less time behind the screen and more time delivering the exceptional guest experiences that keep independent properties competitive.

What makes this different: you won’t do it alone. Lighthouse is deploying an agent AI infrastructure — Enablement, Pre-Sales, and Coaching agents — alongside a modern revenue stack. AI handles the prep, the sequencing, and the pattern recognition so you can focus on what matters — building relationships, running sharp discovery, and closing deals.

Where you will have impact

Own your territory and your number. Build and execute a strategic territory plan to generate a net-new pipeline. Maintain 3x pipeline coverage, forecast honestly, and take full accountability for your results. Your quota is your commitment.

Hunt and build a pipeline. Source a meaningful share of your own pipeline through outbound sequences, ICP targeting, Lighthouse Connect events, and industry conferences. This is not an SDR-reliant role.

Run a disciplined sales process. Using MEDDPICC to qualify and advance opportunities. Use the AI Pre-Sales Agent to identify gaps before every major call. Advance deals through stage gates with evidence, not optimism. Leverage AI to make your days easier and focus on more selling time.

Use AI as a force multiplier. Leverage the Enablement Agent for call prep, discovery frameworks, and positioning. Use the Coaching Agent to surface patterns in your pipeline and win rate. Push back on the tools when they’re wrong — help make the system smarter.

Become an expert in the independent hotel market. Understand the unique challenges independent hoteliers face and position the Lighthouse Indy product suite — including Pricing Manager, Channel Manager, Reservation Manager, and Booking Engine — as the integrated solution that replaces fragmented point tools. Build trusted relationships with independent hotel owners and GMs by speaking their language and solving their problems.

Drive results beyond net-new. Consistently meet and exceed sales targets through new business and by identifying expansion and upgrade opportunities within your accounts. Partner with Product to share market feedback and influence the roadmap. Represent Lighthouse at industry events to build the brand and your network.

About our team

You’ll join a global Revenue team of 150+ sales professionals across 24 countries, dedicated to expanding Lighthouse’s presence in the independent hotel market. This team is focused on helping independent hoteliers unlock their revenue potential with tailored solutions. You’ll work closely with SDRs, product specialists, and regional leaders in a collaborative environment that rewards initiative and offers real career growth as we scale our Indies business.

What's in it for you?

• Impactful work: Shape products relied on by 85,000+ users worldwide.

• Competitive compensation: Proactively maintained to value your work.

• Flexible working environment: Work from home or at one of our global offices.

• Flexible time off: Autonomy to manage your work-life balance.

• 401k matching: Up to 4%.

• Health insurance: Two Blue Cross Blue Shield plans with 99% company contribution to the base plan and 75% for dependents and spouses, plus $25/month to HSA.

• Vision and Dental Insurance: Dental Buy-up plan option, 50% company contributions to premiums for both employees, dependents and spouses for both.

• Employee Assistance Program: 100% confidential and free.

• Employer paid Short Term Disability + $50,000 Life Insurance

• Parental leave: 12 weeks of company paid primary caregiver leave, 3 weeks of company paid secondary caregiver leave, $1,500 new parent bonus, and 4 week flexible return to work plan.

• Wellbeing support: Subsidized up to 80% ClassPass subscription.

• Referral bonus: Earn rewards for bringing in new talent.

Who you are

• 2+ years in a closing sales role, SaaS experience is a must but hunger and skill matters more than industry tenure.

• Fully fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal)

• Self-directed, coachable, and driven to continuously improve. You seek feedback on your calls, your pipeline, and your positioning — and act on it within the next deal, not the next quarter.

• You treat AI tools as a core part of your selling motion, not a novelty. You adopt new tooling quickly and bend it to your style.

• Experience with MEDDPICC or similar qualification frameworks is a plus, not a requirement. What matters is that you bring discipline and structure to how you run deals.

• Strong business acumen with the ability to sell on value, not price. Confident engaging stakeholders from GMs to C-suite.

• You want to win. You prospect when it would be easier not to. You follow up one more time. You’re not okay with a bad quarter.

Diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

Thank you for considering a career with Lighthouse. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace that values equal opportunity for all. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds, regardless of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, and disability. Our commitment to equality is part of our culture. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point during the application or interview process, please notify your recruiter.

Not ticking every box? No problem! We value diverse backgrounds and unique skill sets, and we encourage individuals from all walks of life to apply. jobs.title: Manager, Business Development (Austin)
jobs.description:
Apollo.io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world's largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo.io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo.io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on BDR Manager to lead our outbound sales development team and drive real pipeline impact. This is a true frontline role. You’ll be in the trenches daily coaching reps, jumping into calls, reviewing workflows, and helping unblock deals in real time.

Your goal is to build confident BDRs, hit pipeline targets, and create a repeatable outbound motion that works.

Key Responsibilities

• Directly manage a team of BDRs with ownership of daily activity, meetings booked, and pipeline created

• Coach reps through live call reviews, role plays, deal strategy, and outbound messaging

• Run weekly 1:1s, team meetings, pipeline reviews, and performance coaching sessions

• Help reps prioritize accounts, personalize outreach, and execute effective multi-channel prospecting

• Be hands-on with outbound motions across phone, email, social

• Support onboarding and ramp for new hires, ensuring reps are productive fast

• Partner closely with Sales Managers to align on ICP, handoffs, and opportunity quality

• Track team performance and quickly course-correct when activity or conversions dip

• Hire, develop, and retain top BDR talent

• Create a high-accountability, high-energy culture focused on growth and results

Requirements

• 4+ years of experience in Sales Development or Revenue roles, with at least 2+ years in a leadership position

• Proven experience coaching individual contributors to quota in a high-growth environment

• Strong outbound fundamentals, you know what good prospecting looks like because you’ve done it

• Comfortable running call coaching, deal strategy sessions, and activity reviews

• Data-informed but people-first, you use metrics to coach

• Experience with outbound tools like Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, etc.

• Clear communicator who can give direct feedback and motivate reps through challenges

• High energy, resilient, and passionate about developing early-career sales talent

The listed Pay Range reflects the total cash compensation inclusive of annual base salary and annual bonus as applicable. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonus target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Apollo and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity; company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; at least 10 paid holidays per year, flex PTO, and parental leave; employee assistance program and wellbeing benefits; global travel coverage; life/AD&D/STD/LTD insurance; FSA/HSA and medical, dental, and vision benefits.

Annual Pay Range

$169,900—$212,000 USD

We are AI Native

Apollo.io is an AI-native company built on a culture of continuous improvement. We’re on the front lines of driving productivity for our customers—and we expect the same mindset from our team. If you're energized by finding smarter, faster ways to get things done using AI and automation, you'll thrive here.

Why You’ll Love Working at Apollo

At Apollo, we’re driven by a shared mission: to help our customers unlock their full revenue potential. That’s why we take extreme ownership of our work, move with focus and urgency, and learn voraciously to stay ahead.

We invest deeply in your growth, ensuring you have the resources, support, and autonomy to own your role and make a real impact. Collaboration is at our core—we’re all for one, meaning you’ll have a team across departments ready to help you succeed. We encourage bold ideas and courageous action, giving you the freedom to experiment, take smart risks, and drive big wins.

If you’re looking for a place where your work matters, where you can push boundaries, and where your career can thrive—Apollo is the place for you.

Learn more here!

jobs.title: Director of Security & Guest Protection
jobs.description:
Director of Security & Guest Protection

About Extrity Services

At Extrity Services, we redefine security by placing a premium on emotional intelligence, de-escalation, and cultivating a thriving company culture. We believe that security goes beyond physical safety; it's about creating an environment where everyone feels secure and valued. We are the leading provider of unarmed and armed security solutions; we pride ourselves on delivering top-notch, reliable services to a wide range of clients. Our commitment to operational excellence, stringent standards, and meticulous attention to detail is what sets us apart from the competition. Join us at Extrity Services, where security is a collaborative effort that values emotional intelligence, embraces de-escalation techniques, and celebrates the unique culture of each client. Together, let's redefine what it means to feel secure.

About the role

The Director of Security & Guest Protection is the senior on-site leader responsible for physical security, protective operations, emergency readiness, guest privacy, incident management, and security-related vendor coordination for a confidential luxury hospitality campus. The property includes guest accommodations, private cottages, dining, spa and wellness facilities, event venues, outdoor activities, service roads, remote areas, and 24/7 operations.

This leader must combine disciplined security judgment with refined hospitality. The security program should feel discreet, calm, approachable, and reassuring while remaining operationally effective. Success requires strong planning, professional writing, executive communication, command presence, and consistent follow-through.

Location: On-site at a confidential 300+ acre luxury hospitality campus in the Franklin/Brentwood area, Tennessee

Employment: Full-time leadership role with flexible schedule and on-call responsibility

Reports to: Senior Property Leadership

Direct reports: Security supervisors, security professionals, and event or contract security as assigned

Schedule: Centered on business and operational planning hours, with flexibility for early mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, major events, VIP movements, and emergencies. The role carries an on-call leadership responsibility and is not designed as a routine overnight shift-manager position.

Security leadership scope

The Director owns the security decision, risk assessment, documentation, escalation, interim safeguards, vendor coordination, and verification that security-related corrective work is completed. Facilities, Engineering, Information Technology, licensed contractors, and public authorities retain responsibility for technical diagnosis, repair, inspection, testing, and certification within their disciplines. You will support these functions in their work and in diagnosing property challenges.

Security program leadership

• Lead the campus physical-security and protective-operations program, including staffing, shift leadership, fixed posts, patrol strategy, overnight coverage, relief planning, escalation authority, and command structure.
• Maintain risk assessments, threat and vulnerability reviews, post orders, patrol plans, access rules, and security operating criteria for guest, employee, event, service, and remote property areas.
• Advise senior leadership on risks, staffing, protective measures, service impacts, costs, and operational tradeoffs.
• Maintain a calm, visible, approachable, and hospitality-centered security presence consistent with a luxury guest environment.

VIP and high-profile guest protection

• Own the tiered VIP and high-profile guest protection program and recurring guest-risk review process.
• Prepare advance plans when notice allows, including risk context, aliases, need-to-know distribution, arrival and departure routes, transportation, escorts, access considerations, staffing, and emergency contingencies.
• Coordinate with executive-protection agents, family offices, tour management, drivers, personal assistants, private staff, and law-enforcement partners.
• Implement discreet and proportionate protective measures that do not draw unnecessary attention to the guest or disrupt other guests.
• Enforce strict confidentiality, no-photography expectations, secure communications, and need-to-know handling of names, aliases, locations, schedules, and incidents.

Major events, logistics, and business continuity

• Review event resumes, production schedules, occupancy forecasts, transportation plans, vendor requirements, outdoor activities, and weather risks to identify security and continuity needs.
• Develop plans for access control, credentials, deliveries, staging, parking, valet flow, shuttles, traffic, vehicle and key control, road restrictions, guest movement, emergency lanes, and overnight asset protection.
• Establish the operating cadence for major events, including advance meetings, written plans, briefings, command-post rhythm, leadership updates, issue escalation, situation reports, and post-event debriefs.
• Preserve regular lodging, spa, dining, activity, farm, and guest operations while supporting large groups, productions, and high-profile programs.

Emergency management and fire/life-safety coordination

• Maintain and improve emergency plans for fire, medical events, severe weather, utility interruption, missing persons, bomb threats, suspicious items, active threats, demonstrations, hazardous conditions, and other credible scenarios.
• Lead the property's internal incident-command structure until public-safety authorities assume command, using disciplined communications, accountability, and clear decision authority.
• Coordinate fire-alarm and life-safety response with Facilities and Engineering, fire departments, alarm monitoring and service providers, inspection vendors, and property leadership.
• Ensure evacuation, sheltering, accountability, emergency access, radio discipline, public-address messaging, and responder reception are planned, trained, and exercised.
• Maintain an impairment and escalation log, establish interim safeguards, and verify that corrective work is closed by the responsible technical owner.
• Plan and facilitate tabletop exercises, silent drills, functional drills, and after-action reviews across departments.

Incident, investigation, damage, and corrective-action management

• Lead or oversee response to security, safety, guest, employee, vendor, vehicle, property-damage, theft, suspicious-activity, and conduct incidents.
• Ensure timely and objective documentation; preserve video, photographs, access logs, key records, witness statements, and other evidence; and maintain appropriate confidentiality.
• Apply clear leadership-notification thresholds and provide concise preliminary, follow-up, and final reports.
• For property or vehicle damage, coordinate estimates, responsible-party information, insurance or payment recovery, vendor access, repair status, and final closure documentation with Finance and Facilities or Engineering.
• Conduct root-cause analysis, assign corrective actions, track owners and due dates, and verify that controls are effective.

Security systems, vendors, and asset control

• Oversee operational use and governance of video surveillance, access control, electronic key management, intrusion and duress alarms, fire-panel awareness, radios, mass notification, visitor and vendor controls, and incident-reporting systems.
• Manage security-related vendor relationships, service calls, scopes, quotes, scheduling, site access, issue escalation, documentation, and completion verification.
• Partner with Information Technology and Facilities or Engineering on integrations, network dependencies, repairs, upgrades, maintenance windows, and system resilience without assuming their technical ownership.
• Maintain inventories, access permissions, audit trails, key and radio accountability, and appropriate retention of video and security records.
• Evaluate new security technology and present business cases, options, risks, costs, and implementation plans to leadership.

People leadership, training, and hospitality

• Recruit, onboard, coach, schedule, develop, and retain supervisors and security professionals who can deliver both safety and exceptional hospitality.
• Set standards for appearance, language, radio etiquette, guest assistance, de-escalation, emotional intelligence, privacy, discretion, and guest recovery.
• Maintain a documented training program covering emergency response, medical response, fire, severe weather, active threat, missing persons, aggressive behavior, VIP handling, systems, patrols, and incident reporting.
• Use scenario-based training, tabletop exercises, coaching, report review, and corrective instruction to build confident decision-making under stress.
• Manage performance, attendance, scheduling, overtime, succession, and supervisory development with People or Human Resources and operations leadership.

Governance, metrics, budget, and executive communication

• Develop and manage the security operating budget, staffing forecast, special-event costs, vendor spend, equipment needs, and annual priorities.
• Build dashboards and recurring reports covering patrol and post adherence, response and resolution times, incident quality, corrective-action closure, training, staffing, overtime, guest interaction, property damage, and emerging risks.
• Lead or actively support the property safety committee and convert incident trends into preventive actions, training, and policy improvements.
• Maintain current security plans, SOPs, emergency plans, maps, checklists, contact lists, post orders, decision trees, and executive briefs.
• Communicate clearly with executives, department heads, frontline teams, vendors, responders, guests, and external security partners.

What you will bring

• Eight or more years of progressively responsible physical-security, protective-operations, emergency-management, law-enforcement, military-security, hotel-security, corporate-security, or comparable experience.
• At least three years leading supervisors and a multi-shift security operation, with responsibility for staffing, performance, training, incident command, and service delivery.
• Demonstrated experience protecting a luxury hospitality, private estate, resort, corporate campus, healthcare campus, entertainment venue, mixed-use property, or similarly service-sensitive environment.
• Experience planning for VIPs, executives, celebrities, public figures, or other high-visibility individuals, including coordination with external protective teams.
• Strong command of emergency planning, incident command, evacuation and shelter operations, fire and life-safety coordination, and drills.
• Demonstrated ability to create professional security plans, SOPs, post orders, incident reports, diagrams, dashboards, and executive presentations.
• Working knowledge of video surveillance, access control, key management, alarms, radios, mass notification, visitor management, and security-reporting platforms.
• Strong judgment, discretion, service orientation, written communication, verbal briefing, and cross-functional coordination skills.
• Valid driver's license and ability to meet all background, licensing, and registration requirements applicable to the position.
• Ability to work on-site and adjust the schedule for evenings, weekends, holidays, VIP stays, major events, critical incidents, and emergencies.
• Ability to walk varied terrain, travel across the campus by approved vehicle or cart, work in changing weather, and respond to incidents throughout the property, including indoor, outdoor, remote, event, service, guest-facing, and back-of-house environments.

Preferred qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in security management, criminal justice, emergency management, hospitality, business, or a related field; equivalent experience is acceptable.
• ASIS Certified Protection Professional (CPP), Physical Security Professional (PSP), or comparable professional certification.
• FEMA ICS-100, ICS-200, IS-700, and IS-800 training; current CPR, AED, and First Aid certification.
• Prior hotel, resort, private-club, private-estate, executive-protection, or high-end event-security leadership.
• Experience managing vendor contracts, service-level expectations, budgets, capital requests, and security technology implementations.
• Tennessee security registration or the ability to obtain it; armed registration is preferred only if the final position requires carrying a firearm.

What success looks like

• Hospitality-centered security judgment that protects people and property without creating unnecessary friction or alarm.
• Strict discretion and confidentiality with guest, employee, incident, and operational information.
• Strong planning and writing that convert incomplete information into clear plans, maps, briefings, checklists, and executive recommendations.
• Calm command presence and timely decision-making during emergencies and high-pressure events.
• Cross-functional influence across Operations, Guest Services, Events, Food and Beverage, Transportation, Facilities, Grounds, People, Finance, and Information Technology.
• Ownership and closure: tracking issues through decision, assignment, repair or corrective action, verification, documentation, and final closeout.

Compensation

Anticipated base salary: $95,000–$110,000, depending on experience, certifications, final scope, and the total compensation package. Benefits, incentive compensation, relocation support, vehicle or phone allowances, and on-call expectations will be defined by the hiring employer.

Equal opportunity

The hiring employer is committed to equal employment opportunity and considers qualified applicants without regard to legally protected characteristics. Reasonable accommodations will be considered in accordance with applicable law.

jobs.title: BNA/CNA Training Class - November 2026
jobs.description:
Nursing Assistant Training

Miller's is proud to provide training for those interested in a career as a Certified Nursing Assistant free of charge. Each student is required to complete class room training and clinical training. Upon completion, students must pass the state exam to become a Certified Nurse's Aide. See below for more details on training.

Classroom Instruction

Each student is required to complete 36-40 hours of classroom work. All students are required to pass (with 80%) all of the tests administered during the classroom portion. (Each student has 3 attempts to pass)

If a student does not pass the classroom phase of the course they will not be placed into the clinicals.

Clinical Practicum

Each student is required to complete 75 hours of supervised practicum in a long-term care facility. During the practicum, the student must perform all required skills successfully. The first 16 hours of practicum is with the class instructor. Absence during this time will result in being excused from the program.

During the practicum, the student may be assigned to work with a preceptor who will assist the student in organization and time management. At the completion of the program the preceptor as well as the instructor will be given an evaluation sheet to complete regarding the students progress during the clinical.

All skills checklists booklets (RCP’s) not signed during the classroom must be demonstrated and signed off during the clinicals by the clinical instructor, or other licensed nursing professional. Completed checklist (RCP) must be submitted at the completion of the clinicals with all required skills completed or will not be eligible for the required state exam.

A “clinical sign-in record” is supplied to each student. This form must be completed by the student and signed by a qualified licensed professional on a daily basis. The student must include the following information on the sheet: date and actual hours worked, signature of student, cosigned by licensed supervisor.

Additional Information

Students are required to pass a criminal background check along with a TB test and physical prior to starting the course. Attendance to all classroom sessions is mandatory in order to meet the program requirements as set by the Indiana State Department of Health. Unsatisfactory performance or attendance issues may result in dismissal from the course/program. Students should check with the facility for details on the dress code requirements.

jobs.title: Manager, Marketing I/II Oncology
jobs.description:
The Marketing Manager I/II – DTC Patient Marketing will be a key driver of Elahere direct-to-consumer and patient-facing marketing strategies. Elahere is the first FDA-approved ADC for FRα-positive, platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer — representing a transformative therapy for a patient population with significant unmet need.

This role is responsible for developing, executing, and optimizing patient-directed promotional programs and multichannel campaigns that meaningfully connect women living with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer to information about Elahere and FRα testing. The MMI/II will serve as a critical connector between patient insights, brand strategy, HCP marketing, and media execution — bringing the patient voice to the forefront of the Elahere brand.

Key Responsibilities

Patient Marketing Strategy & Campaign Execution

• Develop and execute integrated, multichannel DTC patient marketing plans in alignment with overall Elahere brand strategy, ensuring consistency across paid media, owned channels, digital platforms, and patient support programs.
• Lead development of patient-facing promotional materials including digital advertising, social media content, disease awareness campaigns, and patient ambassador/testimonial programs, from brief through regulatory approval and launch.
• Champion patient-centric messaging rooted in the Elahere efficacy and safety story, including OS benefit (median 16.5 months vs. 12.7 months vs. chemotherapy) and the importance of FRα biomarker testing as a gateway to treatment eligibility.
• Develop DTC messaging frameworks that address the emotional and clinical journey of women with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer — including recurrence, treatment decision-making, and communicating with their oncologist.

Omnichannel & Digital Marketing

• Partner with digital/media agencies to plan, activate, and optimize paid digital campaigns (search, display, social, programmatic, CRM/email, and streaming/video).
• Manage patient website content strategy and SEO/SEM initiatives in alignment with brand guidelines and regulatory requirements.
• Utilize data and analytics to monitor campaign KPIs — including reach, site traffic, patient activation rates, and script lift — and translate performance data into actionable optimization recommendations.

Patient Support & Access Integration

• Collaborate with patient services, market access, and Halo (AbbVie's patient support program) teams to ensure seamless integration of DTC patient acquisition tactics with downstream support enrollment and adherence programs.
• Develop communications that address patient barriers, including FRα testing access, out-of-pocket costs, and ocular toxicity management guidance for patients.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner closely with HCP marketing to develop aligned messaging architectures that reinforce the provider-patient dialogue around Elahere — particularly regarding FRα testing and treatment selection.
• Collaborate cross-functionally with Medical Affairs, Regulatory, Legal, Market Research, and Patient Advocacy to ensure all DTC materials are compliant, scientifically accurate, and patient-centered.
• Serve as the patient marketing lead on the Elahere brand team, representing DTC strategy in brand planning and commercial leadership reviews.

Budget & Agency Management

• Manage DTC patient marketing budget with full accountability for accurate tracking, forecasting, and ROI measurement.
• Direct and manage external agency partners (creative, media, digital) ensuring delivery of high-quality work on time and within budget.

Insights & Market Intelligence

• Commission and synthesize patient-level market research, social listening, and journey mapping studies to generate actionable insights that inform messaging, channel strategy, and creative development.
• Monitor competitive DTC activity in the ovarian cancer space and provide strategic recommendations to brand leadership.

Education

• Bachelor's degree required in Marketing, Life Sciences, Business, Communications, or related field.
• MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.

Experience – Marketing Manager I

• 3+ years of marketing experience, with at least 2 years in pharmaceutical or biotech marketing.
• Prior exposure to oncology, rare disease, or specialty patient marketing preferred.
• Experience developing patient-facing promotional materials and navigating the regulatory/MLR review process.

Experience – Marketing Manager II

• 5–7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical marketing experience, with a minimum of 3 years in oncology or specialty DTC patient marketing.
• Demonstrated track record leading multichannel DTC campaign development and execution, including digital/social media, CRM, and patient support integration.
• Experience working on ADC, biomarker-driven, or companion diagnostic brands strongly preferred.
• Prior ownership of patient marketing within a brand team structure, including leadership of agency relationships and cross-functional alignment.

Skills & Competencies

• Strong strategic thinking and business acumen with the ability to translate patient insights into differentiated marketing strategies.
• Deep understanding of oncology patient journeys, health equity considerations, and the emotional complexity of cancer treatment decisions.
• Proficiency in digital marketing metrics, analytics platforms, and performance reporting.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to develop compelling narratives for senior commercial leadership.
• Demonstrated ability to manage complexity in a cross-functional environment and influence without direct authority.
• Working knowledge of FDA promotional regulations, PhRMA guidelines, and the MLR review process as applied to oncology DTC marketing.
• High level of personal integrity, accountability, and commitment to AbbVie's values.

jobs.title: Process Improvement Specialist
jobs.description:
About Checkr
Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About Checkr

Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Established in 2014, Checkr's innovative technology and robust data platform help customers assess risk and ensure safety and compliance to build trusted workplaces and communities. Checkr has over 100,000 customers including DoorDash, Coinbase, Lyft, Instacart, and Airtable.

We're a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About the Role

As Process Design Specialist, you'll assess how our operations processes work today and identify where they break down or fall short, using established process mapping methods to help design what should replace them. That includes taking customer experiences and turning them into concrete, standardized improvements to our support flows, with support from your manager and senior team members on the larger or more ambiguous calls.

Our ideal candidate is a systems thinker who can look at a process end to end and pinpoint where it breaks down or stops scaling. You bring structure to ambiguity: you can take that understanding and help design something better, not just a cleaner version of the same process. You document what you find clearly, whether that's a process map, an SOP, or a runbook, and you know how to use current tools, including AI, to speed up discovery and documentation without cutting corners on rigor.

We're not just documenting today's process — we're designing for a future where agents handle more of the execution. You'll help define where automation can run end to end and where a human-in-the-loop checkpoint is still required, setting the standard so our processes scale without losing rigor or compliance.

This role reports to the Senior Manager, Operations Knowledge Systems & Process Design, and joins a growing team of knowledge and process specialists. It will require periodic travel (<10%) to connect with teams across Checkr's San Francisco, Denver, and Santiago offices.

What You'll Do:

• Assess existing operations and support processes using established methodologies to identify gaps, redundancies, and inefficiencies, and baseline current performance using existing operational data (volume, handle time, TAT) to size the problem before recommending a change.

• Translate customer experiences into mapped, actionable improvements to support flows

• Map current-state and future-state processes using standard methodologies (process flows, swimlane diagrams, RACI) to produce clear, actionable documentation, with an understanding of FCRA-regulated workflows

• Support the team's intake process for new process improvement requests, so operations teams know exactly what to submit

• Facilitate working sessions with subject matter experts to capture tribal knowledge and convert it into documented, repeatable processes

• Partner with Quality & Training, Operations Insights, and Program Management teams to translate process maps into standardized SOPs, runbooks, and playbooks

• Identify opportunities to apply automation and AI-assisted workflows to reduce manual, repetitive steps in existing support processes

• Track process improvement initiatives from assessment through adoption, escalating risks and blockers as needed

• Measure process changes against the pre-change baseline and report whether the change moved the metric, flagging when a fix hasn't solved the underlying problem

• Collaborate cross-functionally to support adoption of new or updated processes, so they don't just get documented and shelved

What You Bring

• 3+ years of experience in process improvement, business process design, or operations analysis, ideally within a support or operations environment

• Hands-on experience with process mapping methodologies (process flow diagrams, swimlane diagrams, RACI matrices)

• Experience assessing a current-state process using structured methodologies and identifying where it's breaking down

• Experience translating unstructured or tribal knowledge into clear, standardized documentation such as SOPs, runbooks, and intake forms

• Comfort working within support and knowledge systems (e.g., Zendesk, Salesforce, Confluence, or similar)

• Familiarity using AI tools to accelerate process documentation, gap analysis, or workflow audits, with the judgment to know where human review still matters

• Strong facilitation skills, with experience running working sessions to gather requirements from cross-functional stakeholders

• Excellent written communication skills; able to produce process documentation that's clear to both technical and non-technical audiences

• Experience quantifying a process's cost in time, volume, or rework before and after a change, using data from existing dashboards and reports; strong in spreadsheets, including pivot tables and lookups (SQL not required)

• Experience defining and tracking success metrics for a process change, and knowing when a metric improved but the underlying problem didn't

• Preferred: experience improving support operations workflows in a high-volume, customer-facing environment

• Preferred: Lean Six Sigma, BPM certification, or equivalent formal process improvement training

• An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Pay Transparency Disclosure

We use geographic cost of labor as an input to develop ranges for our roles and as such, each location where we hire may have a different range. If this role is remote, we have listed the top to the bottom of the possible range, but we will specify the target range for an exact location when you are selected for a recruiting discussion. For more information on our compensation philosophy, see our website.

On-target Earnings OR Base Salary range (Nashville, TN)

$64,000—$80,000 USD

What We Offer

• A fast-paced and collaborative environment

• Learning and development allowance

• Competitive cash and equity compensation, and opportunity for advancement

• 100% medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Up to $25K reimbursement for fertility, adoption, and parental planning services

• Flexible PTO policy

• Monthly wellness stipend

At Checkr, we believe an in office work environment strengthens collaboration, drives innovation, and encourages connection. Our hub locations are Denver, CO; San Francisco, CA; Nashville, TN; and Santiago, Chile. Individuals are expected to work from the office 3+ days a week. In-office perks are provided, such as lunch five times a week, a commuter stipend, and an abundance of snacks and beverages. A relocation stipend may be available for those willing to relocate to a Checkr hub location.

Equal Employment Opportunities at Checkr
Checkr is committed to building the best product and company, which requires hiring talented and qualified individuals with a diverse set of perspectives and lived experiences. Checkr believes in hiring people of all backgrounds, including those whose histories are impacted by the justice system in accordance with local, state, and/or federal laws, including the San Francisco’s Fair Chance Ordinance.

Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

Within Manufacturing Engineering, Product Engineering supports manufacturability targets by partnering with Research and Development and other cross-functional teams to evaluate product designs and recommend practical solutions for production.

Success in this role requires working knowledge of product design, production processes, and project coordination. The Specialist, Manufacturing Engineering – Interior Assembly supports the manufacturability and production readiness of assigned interior systems and components within General Assembly. You will report to the Sr. Manager, Body System at Production Planning.

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

• Support Design for Manufacturing activities by evaluating assigned interior components against production, quality, safety, and ergonomics requirements.

• Review manufacturing requirements and provide technical input to interior product designs and assembly concepts.

• Coordinate assigned manufacturing topics with Manufacturing, Production Planning, Engineering, Quality, and Production Control partners.

• Analyze CAD data, simulations, and virtual test results to identify manufacturing risks, assembly constraints, and potential quality concerns.

• Document findings, track open issues, and support timely resolution of assigned product and process concerns.

• Recommend and implement approved product or process improvements that reduce rework, improve manufacturability, and support stable production.

• Support trials, builds, and production-readiness activities for assigned interior systems and components.

• Maintain technical documentation, status updates, and deliverables in alignment with project milestones and internal requirements.

• Complete assigned work with general direction, escalating significant technical, timing, or production risks to the appropriate stakeholders.

Location & Travel Expectations:

• This role will be based out of the Scout Motors location in Blythewood, South Carolina

• This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.

• Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

• Travel: Domestic and international travel required, approximate 10% of the time. Valid driver's license required. Passport required.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

• 4+ years of professional experience in manufacturing engineering, production planning, or a related automotive manufacturing environment, preferably within General Assembly.

• Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing engineering, mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, or a related field. An equivalent amount of relevant work experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

• At least 1 year of experience reviewing or working with CAD models and related technical data.

• Working knowledge of vehicle engineering, manufacturing processes, and production-readiness principles.

• Ability to analyze technical information, identify risks, organize priorities, and follow issues through resolution.

• Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships.

• Practical problem-solving skills and sound judgment when working within established processes and technical standards.

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up.  This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation.  In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

• Competitive insurance including: Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans

• 401(k) program with: An employer match and immediate vesting

• Generous Paid Time Off including: 20 days planned PTO, as accrued 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial Base Salary Range: $100,000.00 - $125,000.00

Internal Leveling Code: IC9: Specialist

Notice to applicants:

• Residing in Los Angeles: Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

• Residing in New York City: This role is not eligible for remote work in New York City.

Equal Opportunity

Scout Motors is committed to employing a diverse workforce and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, disability, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected by law. Scout Motors is committed to compliance with all applicable fair employment practice laws. If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please contact ScoutAccommodations@scoutmotors.com.

jobs.title: Principal, Strategy & Operations, Global Revenue Enablement
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

The Global Revenue Enablement (GRE) organization exists to equip every audience in our go-to-market ecosystem—field, partners and customers —with the clarity, systems, and operational leverage they need to execute with machine speed and absolute consistency.

Within frontier AI and high-velocity cloud environments, enablement is fundamentally a systems engineering and operational discipline. Sitting at the nexus of GRE and our Technology & Systems engineering organizations, this Principal TPM serves as the operational architect for our revenue machine. Your mandate is to design, orchestrate, and institutionalize GTM processes built on AI-first principles—eliminating manual friction, automating complex quote-to-cash workflows, and building scalable rails for rapid commercialization.

We are looking for an exceptional Principal TPM who combines top-tier portfolio governance with deep technical, systems, and operational fluency. You operate as an internal principal consultant, systems strategist, and execution engine.

You will partner hand-in-glove with GRE’s Technology & Systems, the Enterprise Technology Team and Data Analytics and AI team, to translate commercial growth strategies into deterministic, automated systems. You will lead high-stakes, enterprise-wide initiatives.

You thrive in high-ambiguity environments, bring order to complex multi-quarter roadmaps, surface critical architectural trade-offs, and align executive stakeholders without needing direct authority.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Design AI-Native Workflows: Partner directly with Technology & Systems engineering to audit, rebuild, and operationalize field and enablement workflows using frontier AI models, automated agents, and intelligent orchestration pipelines throughout the organization.

 - Eliminate Operational Friction: Systematically dismantle manual bottlenecks across the GRE’s lifecycles, e.g. team to team handoffs, vendor relationships, technical business requirements scoping, and enablement content.

 - Intelligent Tooling Deployment: Act as the lead technical sponsor for evaluating, piloting, and standardizing tool stack based on GRE priorities. 

 - Drive High-Impact Projects via Scrum: Lead and execute mission-critical technical programs using rigorous Scrum and Agile methodologies—running sprint planning, backlog prioritization, cross-functional standups, and retrospectives to ensure predictable, high-velocity delivery across distributed GRE teams

 - Enablement as a Product: Treat operational enablement as an engineering-grade platform. Establish program telemetry, operational SLAs, and feedback loops to measure ramp time, operational velocity, and release velocity

 - Portfolio Strategy & Intake: Run the strategic intake and prioritization engine for Technology & Systems team, filtering unstructured business demands into rigorous, measurable delivery roadmaps aligned to top-line outcomes.

 - Executive Program Alignment: Coordinate and drive alignment cross-functionally across teams, managing communications, milestone delivery, and critical risk mitigations.

 - Quote-to-Cash Optimization: Drive the multi-quarter technical program roadmap conversations for CPQ architecture (Salesforce) to accelerate GRE’s service/deal structuring.

 - Packaging & Pricing Execution: Partner with Head of Customer Activation and lead the technical operationalization of enablement services/packaging, and API pricing models.

 - Governance Automation: Partner with Finance, Legal, and Deal Desk to codify pricing rules, custom discounting thresholds, and contractual guardrails into automated rules engines, dramatically reducing manual approval cycle times.

 - Downstream Systems Interoperability: Ensure seamless data synchronization across LMS, CRM, CPQ  and usage-metering infrastructure for real-time contracting and provisioning.

 - Operational Readiness: Ensure all systems (CRM, CPQ, billing, product telemetry, and field enablement repositories) are fully configured, tested, and validated prior to any public or gated release.
   
    


REQUIRED SKILLS:

 - 10+ years of technical program management, business operations, or revenue systems leadership within high-growth technology, SaaS, or frontier AI environments.

 - Proven IC5 Track Record: Demonstrated ability to drive multi-quarter enterprise programs across diverse teams (Engineering, Product, Legal, Finance, and Sales) with minimal direction.

 - AI-First Fluency: Practical understanding of modern LLM APIs and agentic workflow orchestration.

 - Deep Systems Fluency: Advanced expertise in the revenue technology stack: Salesforce (Enterprise CRM/CPQ) and data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery).

 - Analytical Rigor: Ability in querying  to derive insights and validate program ROI.
   
    

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com

As a Head Coach (General Manager), you're the leader, strategist, and mentor of your store. You'll inspire your team, drive operational excellence, and deliver exceptional guest experiences using data-driven insights to build healthier communities through real food.

• Systems, Process + Technology: Operate and support all systems, troubleshoot issues, and prioritize daily operations to ensure smooth business and guest experiences.

• Execute Head Coach Career Path Duties: Perform all essential functions outlined in the Assistant Coach role, including those from the Shift Leader, Kitchen Lead, and Team Member roles.

What Makes You Stand Out

• Experience in high-volume, fast-paced restaurants.

• Hands-on experience with local, organic, and sustainable products

• ServSafe Manager or Regional Manager Food Safety Certification

• Tech-savvy and comfortable using digital tools for operations, reporting, and team communication

• Strong financial acumen: managing budgets, labor, and P&L effectively

• Proven experience hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing teams

• Exceptional adaptability and problem-solving in fast-paced, dynamic environments

• Data-driven mindset with curiosity to identify and implement operational improvements

• Commitment to operational excellence, hospitality, and team engagement

• Experience in fast-casual or retail operations is a plus

Minimum Requirements

• 3+ years in food service, with at least 2 years in hands-on management

• Experience hiring, developing, training, and motivating team members

• Skilled in planning, managing, and forecasting financials, labor, and inventory

.

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

• Superior customer service, teamwork and verbal/written communication skills

That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

jobs.title: Quality Engineer
jobs.description:
Step into the innovative world of LG Electronics. As a global leader in technology, LG Electronics is dedicated to creating innovative solutions for a better life. Our brand promise, 'Life's Good', embodies our commitment to ensuring a happier life for all. We have a rich history spanning over six decades and a global presence in over 290 locations.  Our diverse portfolio includes Home Appliance Solutions, Media Entertainment Solutions, Vehicle Solutions, and Eco Solutions.  Our management philosophy, "Jeong-do Management," embodies our commitment to high ethical standards and transparent operations. Grounded in the principles of 'Customer-Value Creation' and 'People-Oriented Management', these values shape our corporate culture, fostering creativity, diversity, and integrity. At LG, we believe in the power of collective wisdom through an inclusive work environment.  Join us and become a part of a company that is shaping the future of technology.  At LG, we strive to make Life Good for Everyone.

The Opportunity:

To continually strengthen its business and support its growth in North America, LG Electronics is seeking a Quality Engineer I to join our Component Solutions team. This position will support product quality and reliability by conducting product testing, failure analysis, and quality investigations while working directly with customers and internal teams to resolve quality concerns.

The Quality Engineer will serve as an important technical point of contact for assigned customer accounts, helping identify root causes, coordinate corrective actions, and drive continuous improvement. This role will work cross-functionally with Quality Assurance, Sales Engineering, customers, and LG’s global manufacturing and quality teams.

Here is why you should come join our team:

You’ll join a collaborative, global organization where you’ll have the opportunity to directly influence product quality and the customer experience. In this role, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to product testing, failure analysis, customer quality issues, and continuous improvement while partnering with teams across North America and LG operations in Korea, Thailand, and Mexico.

This is an individual contributor position that offers meaningful ownership of customer quality issues, giving you the opportunity to lead investigations, recommend solutions, and see quality improvements through from identification to resolution.

What You’ll Do:

• Perform product and compressor testing to evaluate product performance, quality, and reliability.

• Conduct teardown and failure analysis of returned products and components to identify root causes of quality issues.

• Investigate customer complaints, field returns, warranty claims, and post-production quality concerns, and coordinate appropriate corrective actions.

• Analyze statistical and quality data to identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities for product or process improvement.

• Prepare quality reports, including field return analysis, warranty claim reporting, testing results, findings, and corrective actions.

• Serve as the primary quality contact for assigned customer accounts, responding to quality concerns and providing technical recommendations and solutions.

• Collaborate with internal Quality Assurance, Sales Engineering, and global engineering and manufacturing teams to investigate and resolve product and customer quality issues.

• Recommend and implement improvements to testing procedures, analytical methods, product quality, and manufacturing or assembly processes.

• Identify opportunities to improve quality and manufacturing efficiency while reducing quality-related costs.

• Participate in quality meetings with customers, internal teams, manufacturing locations, and headquarters to communicate findings and coordinate improvement activities.

• Maintain accurate quality records, test results, reports, and supporting documentation.

• Prioritize urgent customer quality matters and initiate appropriate actions while coordinating with management and global quality teams as needed.

Job Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.

• Ability to understand and apply quality assurance principles, testing methodologies, and analytical processes.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including the ability to organize, analyze, and report on quality-related data.

• Strong problem-solving and root cause analysis skills.

• Ability to analyze technical information and quality data to identify issues and recommend solutions.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information to internal teams and customers.

• Ability to work effectively across multiple functions and with global teams.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and respond quickly to urgent customer quality concerns.

• Korean and English bilingual communication skills preferred

• Experience in quality engineering, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, product testing, reliability, or a related engineering environment is preferred.

• Experience performing product teardown, failure analysis, or root cause investigation is preferred.

• Experience working directly with customers on product quality or technical issues is preferred.

• Knowledge of statistical quality analysis and continuous improvement methodologies is preferred.

• Experience with compressors, HVAC, components, mechanical products, or other engineered products is a plus.

• Frequent travel required up to 30% of the time

$60,000—$70,000 USD

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Verifications
jobs.location: Denver, Colorado, United States; San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
About Checkr
Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to help shape the end-to-end experiences that power Checkr’s Verifications products—spanning employment, education, criminal record, and driving record verifications, with a key focus on drug & occupational health testing. You’ll partner closely with Product, Engineering, and cross-functional stakeholders to design intuitive workflows for complex, high-trust domains—balancing candidate ease, employer clarity, and operational realities.

This is a hands-on product design role with high ownership: you’ll drive discovery through execution, bring strong craft, and help the team make great decisions through clear thinking and excellent communication.

What you’ll do

• Own design for key Verifications product areas—including drug & occupational health testing—across candidate, employer, and internal operational experiences (as applicable), from discovery through launch and iteration.

• Partner with Product and Engineering to define problems, shape roadmaps, and deliver high-quality solutions that align user needs with business outcomes.

• Simplify complex workflows (verification requests, document collection, consent/authorization, appointment scheduling, status visibility, exception handling) into clear, user-friendly experiences.

• Use AI-assisted design and development tools to rapidly prototype, validate, and—when appropriate—implement lightweight UI changes in code to improve iteration speed and overall product quality.

• Design for trust and clarity in a sensitive, regulated domain—prioritizing transparency, error prevention, accessibility, and confidence-building UI patterns.

• Translate insights into outcomes by combining qualitative research, stakeholder input, and product data to propose, test, and refine solutions.

• Create thoughtful interaction and visual design across responsive web and/or platform surfaces, producing clear specs and assets for engineering.

• Facilitate alignment with workshops, design reviews, and strong storytelling—helping teams move from ambiguity to decisions.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with partners such as Customer Success, Sales, Compliance/Legal, Data, and Operations to ensure designs work in the real world.

• Contribute to design systems and standards to improve consistency, speed, and quality across Checkr.

What you bring

• You have 5–8+ years of product design experience (or equivalent), with a strong track record of shipping high-quality work.

• Your portfolio demonstrates end-to-end thinking: problem framing, exploration, rationale, collaboration, iteration, and measurable impact.

• You’re comfortable working in complex domains where edge cases matter, and you can distill that complexity into simple, usable flows.

• You have strong product instincts—you know how to balance user needs, business goals, technical constraints, and timeline realities.

• You’re experienced in collaborative, cross-functional environments, influencing decisions through clarity rather than authority.

• You can independently plan and execute lightweight research (interviews, usability testing, concept validation) and partner effectively with researchers when available.

• You sweat the details: interaction patterns, content clarity, information hierarchy, and accessibility best practices.

• An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Nice to have

• Experience in background screening, HR tech, healthcare, identity, compliance-heavy, or other high-trust regulated spaces.

• Experience designing B2B / B2B2C products, especially workflows used by operations teams or external partners.

• Familiarity with design systems, documentation, and scalable component thinking.

• Experience designing for secure data, consent, and privacy-forward user experiences.

If this role is remote, we have listed the top to the bottom of the possible range, but we will specify the target range for an exact location when you are selected for a recruiting discussion. jobs.title: Product Manager, Fulfillment
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.

We’re helping businesses get off the ground by enabling them to focus on running their business. We solve HR issues. We’re data-driven and never stop iterating. If you’d like to work in a supportive, entrepreneurial environment, are interested in building something meaningful and having fun while doing it, we’d love to hear from you.

We're united by shared goals and shared motivations at Justworks. These are best summed up in our company values, which are reflected in our product and in our team.

Our Values

If this sounds like you, you’ll fit right in.

About the team / Product at Justworks

The Justworks Product team advances our mission by building products that extend levels of personal care and deep expertise that our customers have never experienced before. We craft innovative solutions that guide users through the most complicated challenges of running (and working for) a small business, with ease. We deeply understand complex regulatory spaces like FinTech, Healthcare, and HRTech, and have a keen intuition for how to connect threads across our customers’ needs and our business’ risk management and commercialization strategy. Our Product Managers lead highly collaborative creative endeavors, bringing together stakeholders across engineering, design, data services, operations, and customer-facing teams to deliver tangible value.

By joining us, you’ll be part of an experienced team of Product Managers who have a proven track record of building large-scale software products that impact small businesses worldwide.

About the role

The Fulfillment team plays a critical role in delivering a seamless benefits experience by building and maintaining the integrations that connect Justworks with external insurance carriers and benefits systems. We develop scalable, reliable solutions that streamline benefits enrollment, improve operational efficiency, and enable accurate data exchange across complex systems. Our work powers the infrastructure behind our benefits offerings, helping ensure that customers and internal teams can confidently manage benefits administration.

As a Product Manager of Fulfillment, you’ll play a high-impact role by driving the roadmap of a team core to the delivery of our mission. You’ll focus on defining and prioritizing initiatives that improve carrier integrations, strengthen our benefits infrastructure, and enable more efficient internal operations. You'll work closely with engineering and operations teams to translate complex technical and business needs into well-scoped solutions, balancing immediate operational priorities with long-term platform scalability.

As a champion for your team’s focus and productivity, you’ll establish clear priorities, manage scope, and remove obstacles to ensure maximum, high-quality output that aligns with Justworks’ business objectives. You will operate independently within your scope, develop a deep understanding of our technical integrations and operational workflows, and clearly articulate the reasoning behind your decisions to your peers and cross-functional stakeholders.

Responsibilities

• Demonstrate ownership for the products and integrations you build and an understanding of shipping reliable, scalable services that support Justworks’ benefits infrastructure

• Shape the strategy and roadmap for key Fulfillment initiatives, balancing operational needs, technical investments, and long-term platform opportunities while articulating a compelling vision of business impact to stakeholders

• Partner deeply with engineering to understand carrier integrations, APIs, and technical dependencies, investigate and prioritize issues, and make informed tradeoffs around scope, sequencing, and implementation

• Collaborate closely with operations and cross-functional teams to understand internal workflows, identify unmet needs, and translate business requirements into actionable product solutions

• Define clear requirements, success criteria, and scope boundaries for initiatives, proactively identifying edge cases and ensuring solutions address both technical and operational needs

• Actively hone your knowledge of the PDLC, from discovery through delivery and iteration, while identifying opportunities to build reusable capabilities and improve existing processes

• Build strong relationships across teams by demonstrating curiosity, empathy, and a commitment to customer-centered partnership

• Contribute to team problem-solving and actively support or facilitate team processes and ceremonies

• Take on opportunities beyond core responsibilities to support broader benefits platform strategy, improve integration capabilities, and drive impact

What you’ll need

• Minimum of 2 years of product management experience in a modern technology business or equivalent experience in software engineering, data science, or business analytics

• A strong commitment to problem-solving, capable of breaking down complex technical and operational challenges into clear, actionable priorities for team execution against business needs

• A willingness to deeply understand the fundamentals of our business model, technical architecture, and operational workflows, prioritizing your own education and development through collaboration with engineers, coworkers, customers, and stakeholders

jobs.title: Research Associate I – Plant Bioassays
jobs.description:
About Pivot Bio:

Fueled by an innovative drive and a deep understanding of microbiology, genomics, crop nutrition and agriculture, Pivot Bio is pioneering game-changing advances in fertilizer technology. Our first commercial product harnesses the power of naturally-occurring microbes, modern gene editing and application technologies to provide nitrogen to crops.  We are dedicated to providing new solutions for farmers to improve yield as they work to help feed the world’s growing population. Read/Hear more about Pivot Bio on Forbes or PBS News Hour.

Reporting to the Plant Bioassay Team Lead, the successful candidate will support the execution and development of greenhouse and controlled environment plant assays evaluating the performance of Pivot Bio’s microbial nitrogen-fixing technologies. The team’s key objective is to generate high-quality, reproducible in-planta data that supports candidate advancement, product characterization, and field performance prediction. This role will contribute to the development and scaling of plant assay workflows, microbial screening pipelines, and experimental data generation to support product innovation and validation.

This role is a 6 month Temporary position and onsite at our Creve Coeur, MO location.

Essential Functions

• Conduct and support execution of in planta assays in greenhouse and growth chamber environments with minimal supervision

• Support the scaling, optimization, and standardization of experimental assays to enable higher-throughput biological discovery pipelines

• Grow, plate, quantify, and maintain microbial cultures using aseptic technique and standard microbial enumeration methods

• Collect, accurately record, and analyze experimental and phenotypic data using LIMS or structured electronic data capture systems

• Attend and present data in R&D meetings and contribute to experimental planning and troubleshooting discussions

• Maintain detailed experimental records and support development or refinement of assay SOPs

Competencies

Knowledge & Application

• Understanding of plant physiology, development, and stress responses

• Familiarity with plant phenotyping approaches and greenhouse plant management

• Basic statistical analysis and data interpretation

Complexity & Problem Solving

• Strong attention to detail with demonstrated ability to accurately document and reproduce experimental workflows

• Applies scientific reasoning to interpret unexpected results

Collaboration & Interaction

• Strong problem-solving and team collaboration skills

• Excellent communication skills and ability to work independently

Required Education & Experience

• Bachelor of Science degree in Biology, Plant Science, Agronomy, Microbiology, or related field

• Hands-on experience greenhouse/growth chamber research (industry or academic research experience acceptable)

• Experience with plant-microbe interactions or microbial culturing techniques is preferred but not required

Must be authorized to work in the United States

About Decagon
